content: A Russian SU-27 fighter flew in a provocative manner towards a US RC-135U aircraft conducting a routine mission over the Sea of Okhotsk, demonstrating air-to-air missiles, amid escalating tensions over Ukraine. This incident followed another close encounter with a Russian fighter jet over the Black Sea, and US President Barack Obama's condemnation of Russian "aggression" in Ukraine.

The heir to the British throne, Prince Charles, and his wife Camilla, are embarking on a 12-day tour that includes a stop in 12 towns and cities across Australia and New Zealand, marking his 15th visit to Australia where they will meet the Australian Prime Minister, and celebrate his 67th birthday with a barbeque in Western Australia.
A 70-year-old woman was attacked in Sneem, County Kerry, and a man is now detained and being questioned at the Killarney Garda (police) station after being apprehended on Saturday morning.
Former GP Hugh McGoldrick, accused of falsifying drug trials on sleep disorder patients, had his name removed from the medical register after a 28-day appeal deadline passed without submission.
A 21-year-old male is under police custody for suspected murder while authorities await the results of a post-mortem examination on a body found near a housing estate in Dorking, Surrey.

Josh Hanson died after being stabbed in RE bar in Eastcote, Hillingdon, and Scotland Yard is urging people who were at the bar after midnight or in the surrounding area at around 1 AM to contact them with information, as no arrests have been made yet.

The company, Hovertravel, is exploring the potential of launching a new tourism-boosting ferry service between Sandown and Southsea, subject to necessary permissions, with discussions underway between Hovertravel and the Isle of Wight Council regarding the details and use of Sandown Beach for the service.

A 30-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of a violent attack in the Heights area involving up to eight assailants, but has since been released pending further investigations, with police urging for any potential witnesses to come forward with information.

Floods in India's northeastern state of Assam have resulted in the death of more than 100 people, affected 450,000 people, and displaced numerous residents, with PM Narendra Modi planning to visit the area to seek a permanent solution to the annual flooding. Meanwhile, some affected people in Gujarat are returning to their villages.

The 25th anniversary season of the Premier League, starting with Arsenal hosting Leicester City on Friday 11 August, will be broadcast on Sky Sports, with Sky Sports screening 10 Friday night games following a multi-million pound deal with the Premier League, while a BBC survey indicates that over a third of Premier League football fans regularly watch matches live online via unofficial streams.

Professional footballer Cristian Montano, aged 22, was arrested by the National Crime Agency for spot-fixing investigations and subsequently dismissed from Oldham Athletic Football Club following a thorough inquiry. The club made the decision swiftly, taking the matter seriously, and the director Barry Owen expressed that it was a difficult week but necessary for the football club's progress.

A 20-year-old man was given a suspended jail term and a supervision order for starting a fire at a former Pontins resort in Brixham, England in 2014, causing extensive damage, including the demolition of the arcade area and significant damage to the pool area and ballroom, and increasing the final cost of demolition due to the presence of asbestos.

In August 2013, former Forest player Grant Wilson returned to the Championship side from Celtic for £2.5m, but has been sans team since his release in May, having made 51 appearances at Forest following two previous spells with Preston North End and Notts County.

Australia's left-arm seamer Faulkner took 3 wickets for 45 runs in the 46th and 48th overs, including the pivotal wickets of Mathews and Perera, while Amila Aponso took 4 wickets for 18 runs as Sri Lanka made 288 and Australia was bowled out for 206, resulting in a 82-run win and leveling the series at 1-1.

Sale rugby coach Steve Diamond confirms that Vadim Cobilas, out of contract in the summer, is moving to France's Top 14, while David Seymour, Will Addison, and Mark Jennings are in advanced talks for new deals, with Chris Cusiter and Tommy Taylor's futures uncertain. Diamond also mentions ongoing recruitment for the next season.

Despite a promising start with Shikhar Dhawan and Virat Kohli making centuries, India ultimately collapsed from 277-1 to 323 all out against Australia's Kane Richardson during a match at Manuka Oval, threatening the World Cup holders' 18-game unbeaten run on home soil. Australia are now 4-0 up in the series and aiming for a whitewash in the final match in Sydney.

A fire at a 24-storey building in London has prompted the temporary suspension of parts of the Hammersmith and City Line and Circle Line due to concerns about debris potentially falling onto the tracks, at the request of the London Fire Brigade; current estimates suggest 58 fatalities but the number may increase.

Scottish footballer Jamie Hamill, 27, who previously played at Kilmarnock's Rugby Park, has signed a three-year contract and will make his second debut there after being released from Scottish Premiership struggling club Hearts. Ayrshire-born and a former Scottish Under-21 international, Hamill was part of the Hearts team that was relegated during his three-year spell. He had initially emerged from Kilmarnock's youth academy.
Ipswich fan Ross Morgan created a hole in his ceiling while celebrating a goal scored by Paul Anderson in the Ipswich v Norwich match, with Anderson later offering to pay for the repairs.

Retailers in Wales are now legally required to keep tobacco products out of public view, with violators facing fines and imprisonment, in a bid to reduce the appeal of smoking and improve public health.

A 20-year-old footballer named Lucas, who has scored three goals in ten appearances with the National League side and is known for causing difficulties for defenses, joins a growing confident Bristol Rovers squad, offering mores options for the manager in the forward areas.

Knaresborough station in North Yorkshire is undergoing renovation, involving making it watertight, removing and rebuilding the chimney stack, and repairing the platform canopy, with work being done at night to reduce inconvenience, as it is considered a historically significant station.
A former NFL player, Lawrence Phillips, died by suicide at age 40, having faced a life of legal troubles and prison sentences following his NFL career, which was marked by on- and off-field issues.

The article presents Mr. Hazzard's proposal for the Belfast Rapid Transit (BRT) plan, which aims to extend the operating hours of bus lanes in Belfast, West and East Belfast, Titanic Quarter, from 7:00 to 19:00. This plan, to come into operation in September 2018, was initially based on 12-hour, seven-to-seven bus lane priorities, and includes consultation phases with stakeholders, focusing on creating optimal load and unload times, drop-off and pick-up periods, and the design of proposals to enhance user compliance.

In a match where Real Madrid's Cristiano Ronaldo broke the record for most league goals for his club, Barcelona's Messi, who had not scored in the league this season, came off the bench to score the winner after a set-up from Luis Suarez, thereby extending his record as the all-time top scorer in La Liga with 287 goals.

More than 70 individuals, including players and directors from several clubs in Italy's third and fourth divisions, have been detained on suspicion of engaging in match-fixing, with authorities alleging links to the 'Ndrangheta crime syndicate, with one police officer also implicated. Previous anti-match-fixing investigations have targeted Serie A and B matches.

Spiderling hybrids from Dolomedes plantarius species, hand-reared by scientist Dr Helen Smith, were released into Castle Marshes to create a new population that potentially adapts better to local climate change, supported by Natural England, Suffolk Wildlife Trust, and a BBC Wildlife Fund grant.

The article discusses that with the Partition of India in 1947, two newly independent countries emerged, leading to millions of people becoming refugees, and it highlights the personal story of a woman and her family's experiences during this historical event.

Iva Barr, who has been running marathons for over 30 years and participated in the first London Marathon in 1981, completed approximately 14 miles of the 2023 London Marathon and decided to take an Underground train to Westminster, walking the remaining miles to the finish line on The Mall, stating she had a "great day" and holds no regrets for her decision.
In China's top cities, soaring property demand has driven some young couples to resort to fake divorces to buy more homes, despite intervention from the central bank to curb rising prices.

A 46-year-old landlord, Mr Jones, died at The Blossoms public house in Holyhead, and a 24-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder. The police are managing the situation, and a 14:00 GMT Arriva Bus that passed the Black Bridge area around the time of the incident has been identified as potentially significant. The family of Mr Jones has expressed their grief. Further details about the cause of death and the investigation are pending.

The article invites readers to follow BBC News Entertainment on various social media platforms (Facebook, Twitter, Instagram) or to contact them with story suggestions via email (entertainment.news@bbc.co.uk).

A fatal collision involving a red Ford Fiesta and a white Asda delivery van occurred on the A713 near Carsphairn, resulting in the deaths of two men from Ayrshire; the driver of the Fiesta at the scene and the van driver (Scott Kennedy) who later passed away in the hospital. Police are seeking a witness who saw a white flat-bed pickup truck on the road at the time of the crash.

Australian rower Sarah Tait, who won an Olympic silver medal in the women's pair in 2012, has been diagnosed with cervical cancer and was hailed by her coach and peers for her resilience, inspiration, and impact on women in sport.

Two suicide bombings carried out by the Taliban in Kabul injured several soldiers and civilians, and occurred on the day when Afghan President Ashraf Ghani was authorizing the US troop deal extension in the city, adding to the ongoing violence and ongoing Taliban offensives.

Daimler predicts a significant increase in full-year sales, despite a slower growth in Mercedes sales in China, with confidence in continued growth in major emerging markets, especially China and India, albeit at a lower rate compared to the previous year. The company reports a 6% increase in sales of cars and commercial vehicles in the second quarter, demonstrating continued dynamic growth.

The 10-year-old son of Denmark's Crown Prince Frederik was saved from nearly drowning at Mermaid Beach, Gold Coast, by a lifeguard named Nick Malcolm, who was personally thanked by the Crown Prince, but officials downplayed the incident, with the lifeguard's supervisor stating that the boy might not have survived without the timely intervention.
An elderly man was found deceased in a fire at the intersection of Elgin Road and Inchbroom Road, and the police are investigating with no signs of criminal activity.

Veterans with complex amputation-related issues are now receiving specialized treatment at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre (DMRC) in Surrey, managing by a staff experienced in servicing military casualties with complex trauma injuries. This new programme mirrors the NHS tertiary referral system, aiming to ensure the best possible treatment and knowledge-sharing between the two entities.

Four new speed cameras on a two-mile stretch in Port Talbot have caught around 125 speeding drivers a day since being installed, a decrease from the 700 drivers caught during a trial period, according to the Wales Road Casualty Reduction Partnership. The Partnership aims to educate motorists about the dangers of excessive speed, with enforcement being used as a last resort after considering engineering solutions.

A Manchester-born teacher was arrested in Spain for allegedly taking secret photographs of his students and sending sexually explicit images of minor children to individuals on the internet. The police discovered a large number of such files at his home, including a dedicated folder with photos of one girl. The authorities aim to identify the victims in the photos.

A seven-year-old sturgeon named Steve, originally housed at World of Water in Romsey, Hampshire, survived swimming out during the early February floods and was later discovered at a car wash a mile away with a few bumps and scrapes. The centre's manager is relieved to have Steve back and the fish, used in displays at the shop, is happy to be reunited with its friends.
Comedian and actor Chris Rock has filed for divorce from his wife, Malaak Compton-Rock, after 19 years of marriage; the couple share two daughters, Lola Simone and Zahra Savannah.

There was a collision on a motorway near Tamnamore, between junctions 13 and 14, causing road closures in both directions with long traffic backups, and authorities are providing alternate routes to Belfast and Enniskillen, while encouraging witnesses to contact the police.

The French government, aiming to test Pope Francis's perceived liberal stance on homosexuality, has proposed senior diplomat Laurent Stefanini for the ambassador post to the Vatican, but the Vatican has yet to respond and the prolonged silence is raising speculation of a rejection due to Stefanini's association with France's legalization of same-sex marriage.

The Nasdaq experienced its largest one-day decline since April 2016 due to drops in semiconductor, biotech, and other non-performing stocks, while the Dow Jones and S&P 500 also fell. The drop was accompanied by a decline in US durable goods orders in February, contributing to a lowering of the US dollar against the euro.

In Morocco, Marketa Vondrousova, the Czech number 233, advanced close to the top 100 by beating Estonia's Kontaveit (99) in the final of the Grand Prix Hassan II, while Croatia's Borna Coric, world number 79, claimed his first ATP title by saving five match points to defeat Germany's Kohlschreiber in the final.

Stoke City has signed cameroonian forward Eric Choupo-Moting, their fourth acquisition of the summer transfer window, who has previously played in the Bundesliga, Champions League, and represented both Germany youth team and Cameroon's senior team, including at the 2010 World Cup.

A 56-year-old man with cerebral palsy, Seamus McCollum, died last September at a private nursing home in Randalstown, Maine, but his death was not initially considered a murder case. This changed in April upon the results of an autopsy, and a woman is now being questioned over his death.

Heavy rains have caused severe waterlogging on main streets in a city, forcing closures of offices, schools, and colleges, and affected 80,000 people in nearby Sri Lanka, with at least 10,000 people evacuated, $75m relief fund announced, and rescue and repair works underway in flooded areas due to a depression in the Bay of Bengal.

A McGill's 904 bus experienced a fire outside Largs on the A760 Kilbirnie Road, but luckily, the driver managed to safely evacuate all passengers, including a partially-sighted woman and her mother, and no one was injured. The road was briefly closed but has since reopened, with the burnt-out bus being removed. The passengers expressed gratitude for the driver's swift actions.

Jake Ball, a 25-year-old cricket bowler, is leading Nottinghamshire's bowling attack in the County Championship 2016 with six wickets in each of their first two games, including an impressive display alongside Stuart Broad, and has been praised by the team's coach and director of cricket for his strong form and professional development. However, despite his personal achievements, Nottinghamshire suffered an eight-wicket defeat against Lancashire in their second match.

The article describes the unveiling of a memorial stone, made from Jersey granite and dedicated to 120 men known as "the Jersey Pals" who were killed during the Battle of the Somme, in the French village of Guillemont. The memorial was attended by a delegation including the Lieutenant Governor, Chief Minister, and the Dean of Jersey, and a core from the middle of the stone will be brought back to Jersey to become part of a monument in Royal Square.

Actor John Boyega, who played Finn in Star Wars: The Force Awakens and was formerly part of Theatre Peckham, expressed his gratitude to the theater and stated that he aims to give back as a graduate. The theater's founder believes Boyega will inspire young members.

Thai golfer Aphibarnrat takes a one-shot lead in a European Tour event, with Fitzpatrick matching him shortly after; Luke Donald, Lee Westwood, and several others trail close behind, while Bradley Dredge withdraws due to a viral infection.

Middlesex, despite losing their openers early, built a strong 342-3 lead in the County Championship, with Ashton Agar's partner, Voges scoring his season's first century, and Malan contributing 147 before getting dismissed, leaving Middlesex poised for their first win of the season, with poor weather forecasted for the third day.

A 52-year-old woman died and a 16-year-old boy is critically injured after an incident on Penilee Road, with police previously seeking a 54-year-old man who has since been found in Dumfries and Galloway, and the scene is currently under investigation.

The famed childhood residence of a Beatles member, located at 9 Newcastle Road, Wavertree, was sold for an undisclosed sum in a competitive bidding war, with the successful bidder seeking to remain anonymous. The three-bedroom house, nestled a few streets away from Penny Lane, attracted interest both domestically and internationally prior to the auction.

A 29-year-old man, Aaron Joseph, has been charged for an alleged dog attack that resulted in the death of 52-year-old David Ellam, while he was walking his Yorkshire terrier, Rolo, in Sheepridge, Huddersfield. Joseph also admitted to possessing cannabis on the same day. His trial has been scheduled for 5 February, with request for an earlier date from the Judge Peter Collier QC.
A body believed to be 22-year-old Thomas Bebbington from Shrewsbury was found 10 miles away from the city, near Leighton, and the family has been notified by West Mercia Police.
The article reports that five-week-old otter cubs are currently receiving six feedings per day and are expected to transition to an outdoor enclosure with a swimming pool and live food by the summer.

A 33-year-old mother of four, Joanne Thompson, was found at her Old Mill Court home in Newtownards on Wednesday, and police are seeking witnesses to a disturbance at a nearby bonfire on Monday, as well as any activity around her home on Tuesday night and early Wednesday morning.

A record-breaking number of 2,270 black-tailed godwits spent time on the Scottish island of Tiree this spring, with many of them found in a small field in Kilmoluaig, and some identified as having arrived from France, Portugal, and Spain, during their migration to Iceland for breeding.

Rangers coach Jim Durrant, who previously worked with the first team during multiple tenures of Walter Smith and Ally McCoist, finds himself without a position in the upcoming season as manager Mark Warburton revises his coaching personnel.
A rare albino deer is drawing attention as visitors observe its adaptation process in its new environment.

A 16-year-old student named Asad Khan died three weeks after starting at Beckfoot Upper Heaton School, his family suspecting bullying was a factor, with the coroner considering whether to call a student to testify about Asad's comments about feeling unsafe at school and perceiving life as hard. The inquest will resume next month.

A 350-year-old painting depicting the 1654 coronation ceremony, found at Rokeby Park in England since 1880, has been restored but its origin, the artist, and value remain a mystery; experts do consider it unique given its representation of the coronation.

In the football match between Macclesfield Town and Wrexham, Danny Rowe and Mitch Hancox scored for Macclesfield, making it 2-0. Danny Whittaker added a third for Macclesfield, while Jordan White missed a late penalty for Wrexham, who remained 15th in the table, and Macclesfield moved up to seventh.

A new sponsorship deal between Total, a French oil and gas company, and the Confederation of African Football (Caf) sees Total become the headline sponsor for Caf's 10 competitions, starting with the 2017 Africa cup of Nations finals in Gabon. Specific value details of the deal are currently confidential.

Spain's new coach Lopetegui calls up experienced players Diego Costa and Juan Mata, while Iker Casillas is overlooked, as Spain, under Lopetegui, prepare to face Belgium and Liechtenstein in their World Cup qualifiers, with a squad featuring players like Sergio Ramos, Sergio Busquets, and David Silva, among others.

A deliberate wildfire, spanning over a 5 km area, is currently out of control, spreading across borders, and has resulted in the deployment of multiple firefighting resources; it is one of 435 wildfires reported since May and poses a risk to life and property, as authorities urge the public to help stop the reckless behavior.

Irish cricketer Boyd Rankin, who played for England from 2013-2014, has returned to play for Ireland following a period of inactivity and limited opportunities, aiming to contribute to Ireland's potential qualification for Test status and the upcoming World Twenty20 tournament.

The Northern Ireland Rare Disease Partnership, a collaborative effort between the Patient Client Council and various stakeholders, aims to provide an independent platform for individuals affected by rare diseases, such as Spondylo Ephysial Dysplasia, and their caregivers, to advocate for improved education, services, and support in the region.

Gloucester Cathedral aims to break traditional gender boundaries by introducing girl choristers to its choir, aiming to discover and nurture female talent, starting with auditions in April and a 'come and sing' open day for local youngsters aged 7-12.

Pedro, Chelsea's winger, suffered an injury during a game in Beijing and was hospitalized overnight; he is expected to train with a protective mask after recovering from concussion and will travel back to London, while the rest of the squad is currently in Singapore preparing for upcoming matches against Bayern Munich and Inter Milan.

James Taylor, a former professional cricket player who retired due to a heart condition in 2016, has joined Nottinghamshire's coaching staff to work with their academy and provide one-day cricket advice, while former Northants captain David Sales, known for his over 22,000 runs, will work with the county's batsmen, focusing on technical aspects of their game.

A man was charged with multiple offenses, including assault on police, in an incident witnessed by prescription pick-up participants, including children, on Whiterock Road, and he is scheduled to appear in Belfast Magistrates Court on December 5.

A stranded yacht's engine failed northeast of Muck Island, prompting a volunteer Larne RNLI crew to launch two lifeboats, tow the yacht to Carrick Marina, and successfully rescue the four aboard, showcasing effective coordination between the inshore and all-weather lifeboats.

In an intense match, Ipswich took the lead twice through David McGoldrick and Brett Pitman, but were equalized by Revell from the penalty spot twice, with a late header from Varney securing victory for Ipswich. Both managers expressed varying degrees of frustration and optimism about their team's performances and future prospects.

A bridge collapse on a motorway near Maidstone on August 27 resulted in injuries, dangerous driving charges for a man from Darlington, and caused the main route to the Channel Tunnel and Port of Dover to be closed for multiple days, while the man faces charges of dangerous driving, causing serious injury, and criminal damage.

In Platja d'Aro, a flashmob organized on social media led to public panic when participants stumbled a celebrity chase scenario, causing a stampede and resulting in 11 injuries and 3 hospitalizations. The incident involved 200 people and was orchestrated by several Germans, who were later detained. Local authorities and the president of Catalonia condemned the event for causing unnecessary fear and commended the response from the town council and police.

A two-and-a-half-year-old boy named Jeremiah Regis, who was found dead with over 100 injuries including a bite to the chest, and his family described as "always smiling," has led to the murder charges against Sindyann Regis, 25, and Chevaze Mcgregor, 27. The court case has been set for trial in April.

A large gorse fire on Woodbury Common in Devon has led to injuries and hospitalization, with 20 fire engine crews fighting the blaze, aided by a helicopter, as the area is too vast and resources are stretched due to wind direction and limited water supplies. The incident has led to evacuations and smoke visible from far away, prompting warnings for the public to stay clear.

The British Speedway Promoters' Association has reached an agreement to save a speedway club, with a 15-year lease signed for its Beaumont Park venue. Further meetings are planned to establish the club's management structure, schedule a race night for the 2017 season, and make other arrangements.

Charles Gordon, 51, has been charged with murder in the death of his sister Elizabeth Bowe, 50, who was found injured at her home in St Andrews on Sep 17th and later passed away in Ninewells Hospital. Police are investigating the initial police response to the incident, with a report to be submitted to the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service.

A 29-year-old footballer, previously on loan at Ross County, has been signed permanently by the club for two years, contributing experience and potential for developing younger players, and may be unavailable for the upcoming Scottish League Cup match if international clearance is not received in time.

In Division Two's match between Northants and Durham, Northants capitalized on Durham's fragile batting, dismissing key players for low scores, and ended the day 59-3, 107 runs behind despite losing early wickets. Max Holden (19 not out) and Chesney Hughes (16 not out) prevented further damage, with Hughes making his first Championship appearance since last August in a non-contract, pay-as-you-play basis.

A New Zealand golfer, one shot off the lead, trails joint leaders Brooke Henderson and Lee Mi-rim following the second round of the Sahalee Country Club tournament, with Canada's Henderson, South Korea's Lee, Scotland's Catriona Matthew, Americans Gerina Piller, Brittany Lincicome, and New Zealander Lydia Ko all within striking distance, on a challenging day of play marked by changing weather conditions.

Former footballer Tommy Watson, 56, is set to join Scotland's management team as assistant to Gordon Strachan for the upcoming World Cup qualifiers, having previously worked with Strachan and Mark McGhee in the 1970s at Aberdeen and under Alex McLeish during the Euro 2008 qualifying campaign.

In the ice hockey match, the Belfast Giants took an early lead through Colin Shields but Scott Aarssen equalized late in the first period. Ryan Martinelli and Mark Garside then scored for Belfast, leaving the Giants ahead 3-1 at the end of the second period. Alex Foster later increased the lead to 4-1 before Steve Saviano sealed the victory with five minutes left. Belfast have a game in hand on the second-placed Devils, while the Giants and Manchester Storm are set to clash the following day, with the busy festive period continuing.

Defending champion Jordan Spieth suffered a dramatic collapse on the final day of the Masters by posting a quadruple-bogey 7 on the 12th hole, allowing Danny Willett to become the first Englishman to win since Nick Faldo in 1996.

The article invites readers to share their recent photographs of England, providing methods such as email, Facebook, Twitter, or Instagram, and stating conditions like granting a royalty-free license for publication, while ensuring copyright ownership remains with the contributor. Safety guidelines are also emphasized.

A court heard that the conduct of eye specialist Honey Rose was so far below standard that it was "criminal," as her alleged failure to detect a patient's swollen optic discs during a routine eye test may have led to his death, making his death potentially preventable. The trial is ongoing.

Food price inflation increased in June to 4.9%, exceeding analysts' expectations, partially driven by rising pork prices, yet still below the government's target of 3.5%. This development reduces the likelihood of interest rate cuts in 2013, as China aims for 7.5% economic growth while managing a possible property bubble, according to Bank of America Merrill Lynch economists.

Former Ivory Coast international footballer Cheick Tiote, aged 30, passed away following a collapse during training with Chinese second-tier side Beijing Enterprises on 5 June. His memorial was attended by friends, family, and former team-mates, with Senegal striker Demba Ba describing Tiote as a brother and shared member of their family. Tiote had made over 150 appearances for Newcastle United in seven years before joining Beijing Enterprises in February.

Young rider Yates dropped out of the race with 75km to go on the fifth stage, allowing Sagan to claim his second victory. Pinot moved into second place overall behind leader Quintana, with Thomas advancing to sixth overall for Team Sky ahead of two remaining stages.

Having faced some opposition, fracking firm Cuadrilla received approval in October to proceed with fracking at its Preston New Road site in Little Plumpton. They promise significant investment, job creation, and community initiatives, while promising half the money spent would stay in Lancashire. AE Yates Ltd has been awarded a £1.5m building contract for the site, with work expected to start early next year.

Three 17 and 19-year-old males from north-west London, feared to be planning a trip to Syria, were arrested in Turkey upon their return to the UK, then released without charge after inquiries; this comes weeks after three schoolgirls from east London, also suspected of planning to join Islamic State in Syria, were reported missing and feared to have flown to Istanbul.

Dr. Christopher Davies, a respiratory consultant at the Royal Berkshire Hospital, expressed disappointment over the purchase of a £22.95 blackout blind, which he considered overpriced, while the hospital's management team rejected the quote for a blind that met fire and infection control regulations. The situation is currently under review by NHS England.

Adam King contributed two goals during a 2-0 win over Reading, securing the League title for Swansea's development squad, which compiled a total of 31 wins across all competitions during the 2016-17 season, with the senior team managing to avoid relegation from the Premier League.

The article discusses the natural re-establishment of dunes at Barkby Beach in Prestatyn, following damage from severe storms in December 2013, while also detailing plans by Denbighshire council to create a secondary dune system for increased flood protection, due to concerns about the narrowness of the existing dunes, with discussions ongoing regarding potential collaborations with Natural Resources Wales to further mitigate flood risks at this location.

The FA Cup preliminary round game between South Shields (Northern League Division One) and Bridlington Town (Northern Counties East League) will be streamed live on various BBC Sport digital platforms, including BBC iPlayer, and commented on by Conor McNamara and Danny Webber, with the option to engage with the commentary team via #bbcfacup.

A 38-year-old man sustained serious, non-life-threatening facial injuries in an unexplained, potentially targeted attack on Craigmillar Castle Road, and Police Scotland is seeking witnesses and information about suspicious vehicles or behavior in the area.

A 51-year-old woman, Pamela McLaggan, has admitted to manslaughter of Jonathan Baines, 44, also known as "Willy," following an incident in Gainsborough, Lincolnshire, and has been remanded in custody ahead of sentencing in December.

A 15-year-old boy was physically attacked by a man and woman in their 40s at Patterton station, suffering facial injuries, including an eye injury, and having his mobile phone stolen. The incident occurred on a 23:05 service between Glasgow Central and Neilston, and anyone who was on the train during the altercation before the assault and witnessed those involved is urged to contact British Transport Police.

A 17-year-old from Dewsbury was questioned for suspected terrorism activities under section 5 of the Terrorism Act, following his alleged departure to Syria to join the Islamic State; this incident occurred while his brother, Hammaad Munshi, who was previously arrested at 16 for possessing a guide to make napalm and was the youngest person convicted under the Terrorism Act, was also from the same area.

The GB ice hockey team, including returning netminder Stephen Murphy and several players from the 2015 World Championship (Division 1B) silver medal-winning squad, will compete against Italy, Netherlands, and Serbia in a tournament from February 11-14. The winners of the tournament will advance to the final qualifying stage for the 2018 Winter Games in PyeongChang, Korea. Meanwhile, host club Cortina will play two games against the Belfast Giants during the tournament.

Matthew Perry, known for his role in Friends, is rumored to contribute to a tribute for the show's creator, James Burrows, although it's not a full reunion, according to Lisa Kasteler. The special, featuring Jennifer Aniston, Courteney Cox, Lisa Kudrow, David Schwimmer, and Matt LeBlanc, is set to air on NBC on 21 February, marking the end of Friends in 2004. Meanwhile, Perry is set to return to London's West End with his dark comedy play, The End of Longing, from 2 February to 14 May.

Jones, a veteran footballer with a varied career that includes stints at Manchester United, Preston, Derby, Blackburn, Wolves, Oldham, and Wigan, made 41 appearances for Burnley last season to help them clinch the Championship title, and he started in their Premier League loss against Swansea.

A well-known Italian-Australian lawyer, Joe Acquaro, was fatally shot in Melbourne, with investigators suspecting involvement of underworld bosses due to his associations with crime figures over extortion, drugs, and arms offenses, in a city where traces of past gangland violence persist.

Air France flight 374 departing from Paris to Vancouver was diverted to Glasgow Prestwick after a slight burning smell was detected on board, and a second aircraft was arranged to transport passengers back to Charles de Gaulle Airport.

A severe weather warning for strong winds and heavy rain has been issued for coastal areas and north-western parts of Wales, including Aberporth, Aberystwyth, and Anglesey, as the remains of Hurricane Gonzalo reach Britain, potentially disrupting travel and increasing the risk of surface water affecting roads.

The article discusses concerns surrounding increasing hospital overcrowding, particularly in relation to long wait times for patients, including children like Lilly and Jake, who describes their respective experiences seeking treatment at a children's hospital in Sheffield.

A 64-year-old man, Kenneth David Dickie, died from a serious head injury at the Rockley Park site in Poole, and a 34-year-old man and a 57-year-old woman have been charged in connection with the incident.

Former Manchester United forward Federico Macheda will remain at Nottingham Forest until the end of the season, but the club's attempts to sign midfielder Andre Moritz have been unsuccessful due to contractual complications.

The body of Christopher Huxtable, who had been missing since a building collapse in February, was found and his remains were escorted off the site in a guard of honor. However, two other individuals, Ken Cresswell and John Shaw, remain missing, and their families are still awaiting their return. MP Carolyn Harris expressed condolences for the family of the deceased but also emphasized her concern for the families of the two still missing individuals.

The Bosnia-Herzegovina international is aiming for match fitness after a hernia injury but is doubtful for the upcoming game, while Jordan Cousins is ruled out for the rest of the season with a quadricep injury, and on-loan winger Kazenga LuaLua is a doubt for the visitors. Bristol City aims to win on Friday to overtake several teams, including QPR, to improve their league position.

Astronaut Luca Parmitano, selected by ESA in 2009 and traveling to the International Space Station in 2013, found spacewalking during his mission exhilarating, as he orbited Earth over 2,656 times while traveling more than 110 million km in total, describing the experience as "absolutely fantastic."

A 16-year-old England Knights player, Joe Arundel, who made 44 appearances for his previous team, is joining Hull FC, expressing excitement and some nervousness about the new challenge and the pressure of joining a big club. The club's director of rugby, Shaun McRae, believes Arundel has great potential for future success with Hull FC and England.

Ulster Bank is working to rectify a payment issue affecting approximately 600,000 customers, with the goal of resolving it by Saturday, reassuring customers they will not be out of pocket. This issue is reminiscent of a major IT meltdown experienced by its parent company RBS in 2012.

Australian prop forward Willie Mason, a veteran of 290 NRL games and a 2004 Premiership winner, joins the Dragons Super League team following stints with multiple clubs and international appearances, as the team seeks to turn around a 0-2 start to the season.

The Marine Conservation Society, despite encouraging improvements in pet waste management, applauds owners for using bags, yet calls for proper disposal in dog bins, as overall beach litter decreased this year.

This was considered a significant victory for employment rights by Union leader Dave Prentis.

In the match between Dagenham & Redbridge and Wycombe Wanderers, Wycombe won 3-2 after Josh Passley's dismissal led to an early Wycombe goal, Thompson was also sent off later, Guttridge equalized for Dagenham, and Cowan-Hall secured the victory for Wycombe. Despite the defeat, Dagenham manager John Still remained optimistic about their progress and team performance.

Bee-eaters, native to southern Europe, have nested in Low Gelt Quarry, near Brampton, resulting in multiple chicks that are expected to fledge in the next few weeks. The RSPB has reported an increase in visitors at the quarry's viewpoint, as the public shows interest in observing these birds. This is the second consecutive summer that bee-eaters have bred in the UK.

A man capsized in the River Wey in Guildford, and though a bystander attempted to save him, divers are now searching the river for the missing kayaker. Authorities have warned against entering the river due to a flood warning, especially at popular kayaking spots, and have urged immediate 999 calls if the kayaker is spotted.

A stone thrown by a captive elephant at Rabat Zoo in Morocco fatally injured a child, according to a zoo statement, with the elephant's behavior considered unusual and likely driven by boredom or frustration; the incident comes following three similar but rare incidents in US zoos, as stated in the zoo's statement.

MP for North West Durham, Ms Glass, has joined the shadow cabinet amidst a wave of Labour MP resignations calling for a change in leadership. Her predecessor, Ms Powell, cited the "untenable" position of current Leader Mr Corbyn, despite acknowledging his decency, principles, and kindness. Ms Glass, with a background in education, enters the cabinet amidst calls for a leadership election.

Chelsea lead the English Premier League with 59 points, while five teams, including second-placed Tottenham, Manchester City, Arsenal, Liverpool, and Manchester United, are within striking distance as Chelsea prepare for a challenging away game against Burnley. Chelsea's manager, Conte, cautions against mistakes during the remaining 14 matches and acknowledges Manchester United as a contender, emphasizing the importance of focus and concentration.

A dispersal order has been issued in Llangefni, allowing police to remove troublemakers and underage individuals from the area, aiming to reduce gang activity, antisocial behavior, and protect young people from the harmful effects of alcohol.

Dutch international midfielder Georginio de Roon played 33 games in the Premier League for Middlesbrough in 2016, scoring 5 goals, and manager Garry Monk expresses interest in signing Chelsea midfielder Lewis Baker.

The city council plans to introduce a larger-scale self-service bike scheme in spring 2017, resembling London's 'Boris bikes', with hire stations at various accessible locations and financed through sponsorship, aiming to prevent public expenditure. The new bike scheme is considerably larger than the initial pilot scheme that ended in 2011.

Despite missing both the start of the season and the Africa Cup of Nations due to a back problem that necessitated surgery, Senegal international Sakho is now beginning light training and is expected to need several weeks of pre-season work to build up his strength and fitness before being considered for selection in the Premier League.

The NI Residential Property Price Index shows that overall prices in Northern Ireland are 5.4% higher than in 2015, with the third quarter seeing a 0.8% increase compared to Q2 2020, with Antrim and Newtownabbey district experiencing the largest rise at 7.3%. The smallest annual increases were in Ards and North Down (2.1%) and for apartments (4%), while terraced properties showed the greatest annual increase (7.1%). Approximately 5,200 deals were completed in Q3.

The delivery of huge wind turbine parts on rural roads in Dumfries and Galloway was highlighted, with one successful passage over Bargrennan Bridge and another resulting in an accident with the lorry and cargo ending up in a ditch on the A713.

The Betsi Cadwaladr health board is considering temporarily downgrading services at one of its district hospitals due to a staff shortage, but plans to reduce maternity services at Glan Clwyd Hospital have been temporarily halted by a legal challenge, prompting public consultations and meetings, with residents concerned about potential increased travel for maternity care. The health board maintains any changes are necessary to ensure safety and has launched a dedicated website for public feedback, with public meetings scheduled for September.

Mignon du Preez scored a century for South Africa in an ODI match, helping her team to 272-6, while seamer Masabata Klaas's bowling performance removed Ireland's openers cheaply, leading to Ireland's defeat by 68 runs.

British high jumper Katarina Peake, age 30, aims to break her current Welsh record and qualify for Team GB in the Rio Olympics by achieving a personal best of 4.50m in high jump at the Cardiff International Sports Stadium.

Firefighters battled a 10-hour blaze at a building site in Llanwern caused by a deliberate setting, involving a large quantity of scrapped railway sleepers, with local police investigating the circumstances.

A charity event organized by the Nepal Scotland Association, Mercy Corps, and the city council, featuring a Singing Bowl Concert at St Giles' Cathedral, took place to raise money for the victims of the recent devastating earthquake in Nepal, many of whom are members of the Association.

UEFA's control, ethics, and disciplinary body has imposed an automatic touchline ban on Neil Lennon, Hibs coach, for violent conduct against the referee during a Europa League qualifying match against Brondby, following his dissatisfaction over a disallowed goal. Hibernian is in the process of appealing the suspension.

A fire occurred 1,100m beneath the sea bed at the ICL UK Boulby mine, causing 7 workers to be hospitalized for smoke inhalation, with 11 initially unaccounted for. Polystyrene blocks are believed to have ignited, and the Health and Safety Executive has served an improvement notice on the company, giving them until June 27 to comply. The investigation into the incident is ongoing.

Two British and French tourists were caught naked at the Unesco World Heritage site, Machu Picchu, and questioned for offences against morality; the local authorities are in contact with the British Foreign Office, and no arrests or charges have been made.

On Friday, Croatia international and Barcelona midfielder Ivan Rakitic will sign a contract extension, which includes a £109m buyout clause, following his impressive performances for the team, such as his role in the 6-1 comeback win against Paris St-Germain, and has already made 145 appearances for the club since joining from Sevilla in 2014.

A couple from Halstead suffered life-altering injuries in a two-hour torture incident on April 26, with one perpetrator described as a black man in his 20s, around 5'10" tall, and police continue investigating the "shocking crime."

The Wickerman Festival, scheduled for 25 and 26 July at East Kirkcarswell Farm near Dundrennan, reveals Dizzee Rascal as its opening-night headliner for the year, with a diverse lineup including Martha Reeves and The Vandellas, The Zombies, Big Country, and The Feeling, with the Saturday headliner yet to be announced.

English rugby players Foden (Saints) and Brown (Quins), both 26, are performing well in the Aviva Premiership, with Foden scoring his third try in two matches and Saints beating Quins 24-3. Both players aim to secure a spot in the upcoming England Six Nations squad, with Brown set to return after the 2008 New Zealand tour. Foden hopes Saints will contribute multiple players to the England squad for the tournament, emulating their performance at the 2011 World Cup.

In Dagenham, a motorcyclist aged 22 died after colliding with a Vauxhall Zafira car, leaving a 10-year-old boy in a serious condition and a 7-year-old with minor injuries. The 38-year-old driver of the car was unharmed, and there have been no arrests; witnesses are being sought by police.

Pfizer has agreed to acquire California-based Anacor Pharmaceuticals, the makers of the potential eczema treatment crisaborole, with hopes of achieving $2bn in annual sales if approved by the US Food and Drug Administration. This move is seen as an attractive opportunity to address a significant unmet medical need for eczema patients, with a current lack of safe and appropriate treatments in the U.S., where 18-25 million people suffer from the condition.

A street fight on Oxlow Lane, Dagenham, resulted in the recovery of multiple weapons and the arrest of two teenage boys, with no reported injuries, according to authorities who stated that the seizure of the knives could have prevented further harm or tragedy.
A 23-year-old man from Cardiff was arrested on suspicion of sexual assault following an attack on a 19-year-old woman at Gorsedd Gardens near Cardiff Civic Centre.

Scottish Conservative MSP John Lamont resigned from the Ettrick, Roxburgh, and Berwickshire constituency seat to contest as a candidate in the Westminster by-election, aiming to defeat Calum Kerr of the SNP, and a by-election has been triggered, with additional elections for the local council and Holyrood representative also scheduled in the same timeframe.

The EU, including major producers France and Germany, can now export beef to Canada following Canada's recognition of the EU's successful measures in eradicating BSE and a growing trend in global trade, especially after a Russian import ban and weaker Chinese demand impacted European farm exports, leading to a €500m aid package and street protests by farmers, particularly in the dairy sector, which has been hit hard. The US has similarly resumed importing beef from the EU.

The European Commission plans to sanction nations on a forthcoming tax blacklist if they fail to heed appeals for change, while negotiations continue for a common list of non-cooperative tax havens, with a new crackdown on banks and tax advisers helping clients hide money offshore.

Archaeologists unearthed Bronze Age burnt mounds, remains of pottery, and fragments of kilns for drying grain at Torvean, some of which were linked to heating systems for cooking, washing wool, or small saunas, during the construction of a new road easing traffic flow through Inverness.

Oldham secured a important victory over Southend, with Main scoring the winning goal after Forte's assist, increasing Oldham's cushion above the League One relegation zone, while Southend remain in 13th position.

Actor and Irish language advocate, Lally, renowned for roles in Glenroe, Ballykissangel, Alexander, and The Secret of Kells, passed away peacefully following a short illness, leaving behind his wife Peggy and their children, Saileog, Darach, and Maghnus.

The Derby City Council, seeking to save £79m over the next three years, initially proposed closing Moorways Pool as a cost-saving measure, but subsequently committed to keeping it open for another year, having found savings in back-office areas and restructuring management jobs untouched since 2010. Campaigners were delighted, highlighting the importance of the pool for teaching young swimmers, with closing it would have left only one other public pool in the city.

Children previously resident in Boko Haram-controlled areas have been detained in a military barracks in Maiduguri, without legal process, according to the UN Children's Fund and human rights groups, amid ongoing concerns over undisclosed numbers of minors being held.

The team also signs experienced goalkeeper, Lee Hollis, who played for Motherwell and is expected to fill in following an injury to Neil.

Basketball player Chelsey Lee, 26, who played for Bucheon KEB Hana Bank in the Women's Korean Basketball League (WKBL), is under investigation for allegedly falsifying her and her father's birth certificates to show a South Korean grandmother, which allowed her to play as a foreign player. The WKBL has announced her suspension for life and annulment of her records, and the team's records, ranking, and the league's extra quota for international players with a Korean parent or grandparent will be nullified.

The article discusses a new app that monitors Wi-Fi speeds and provides tips to improve them, while noting that a significant number of homes and offices in the UK are not utilizing their Wi-Fi networks at optimal speeds due to interference from various electronic devices, and suggesting that more needs to be done to address this issue, particularly for those in rural areas and small businesses.

Manchester United player Paul Pogba shared an emoji on advertising boards in response to his performance during the draw against Liverpool, and forward Zlatan Ibrahimovic, who scored the equalizing goal, praised Pogba for thriving under pressure. Ibrahimovic, who has equalized Premier League goal records with Chelsea's Diego Costa and Arsenal's Alexis Sanchez, expressed his desire for team success over personal accolades.

A metal object, discovered floating in a remote river in Salinopolis, Brazil, has been identified as debris from Europe's largest telecommunications satellite, Alphasat, launched from Kourou base in French Guiana last July. The debris, confirmed by the UK Space Agency, is said to be the size of a car and officials are arranging its retrieval.

The article discusses James Purnell's warning that decriminalizing non-payment of the BBC TV license could lead to a £200m loss for the BBC, potentially forcing the closure of BBC Four, CBBC, and CBeebies, and increasing the license fee due to higher evasion rates. The issue of decriminalization will not be discussed until charter renewal talks in 2017. Additionally, a Labor MP has argued against the closure of BBC Three.

In their Premier Division debut, Derry City struggled to contain a resurgent Finn Harps, with Ryan Curran and David Scully scoring for Harps, while Rory Patterson scored in injury-time for Derry, but it wasn't enough to salvage a draw, with Harps earning their first win over Derry since 1998. Ex-Derry players Barry Molloy and Tony McNamee made significant contributions for Finn Harps.

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has stated that securities offered through Initial Coin Offerings (ICOs), using blockchain or distributed ledger technology, must be registered, following concerns over an investment bubble and lack of investor protection. The SEC clarified that existing securities regulations, rather than crypto-currency specific laws, apply to ICOs.

Operation Anagram, initiated by Strathclyde Police in 2006 following the rape and murder of Angelika Kluk, played a pivotal role in convicting serial killer Peter Tobin for the murders of Dinah McNicol and Vicky Hamilton. Despite being scaled back, the operation remains active, providing a platform for information regarding Tobin, who is currently serving three life sentences. The investigation has brought some solace to the families of the victims, offering closure, and will continue to be monitored for potential new leads.

In the Australian Grand Prix, Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel emerged victorious over Lewis Hamilton, with Hamilton acknowledging Ferrari performed better in the race and expressing hope for a turnaround in the upcoming Chinese race. Both drivers agreed that the season will be exciting due to close competition, with Vettel stating that defeating Mercedes is challenging and Hamilton emphasizing that Mercedes remains the favorite.

The Southwark Crown Court is hearing a trial where Mr Clifford, a former celebrity lawyer, is accused of indecent assault in the 1980s. The alleged victim claims he exposed himself, forced her to perform a sex act, and threatened to rape or kill her. Mr Clifford denies the allegation and has given a "no comment" in his police interview, contending that the allegation is untrue. The trial continues with Mr Clifford expected to testify on Monday.

In the given article, Coach Steve Tandy anticipates a physical and intense match between Ospreys and Scarlets, expecting the game to be a spectacle, despite Scarlets having a lead in the Pro12 table, and Nicky Smith being available for Ospreys after recovering from injury.

A massive Diwali celebration took place on the Golden Mile (Belgrave Road) in Leicester, England, known for being one of the largest Diwali parties outside India, and included a fireworks show, Rangoli art, stage entertainment, and various events throughout the city. The festival, celebrating light over darkness, was attended by thousands and was enjoyed by people from diverse backgrounds.

Rosie's Helping Hands charity, established by the parents of Rosie Ross who was tragically killed in 2001, has raised over £350,000 for young people in Aldridge. They plan to wind down the charity after their annual Rosie's Walk in 2017, as next year marks the same amount of time they had with their daughter. The charity has funded a pirate-themed play area on the children's ward at Walsall Manor Hospital, greatly enhancing the environment for sick children.

Macmillan Cancer Support, in conjunction with Cwm Taf Health Board, is seeking planning permission for a new £5m palliative care unit at the Llantrisant site, which would be Macmillan's biggest single investment in Wales, offering inpatient, outpatient, and day care for incurable cancer and other conditions, aiming to provide high-quality care in a comfortable environment and ensuring easier access to specialist tests and treatments at the Royal Glamorgan Hospital.

Northern Wales is recognized as one of the top 10 travel destinations in the world by Lonely Planet, featuring landmarks such as Surf Snowdonia, Zipworld's Penrhyn Quarry zip line, and Snowdonia National Park. The Welsh government has confirmed that the number of tourists coming to Wales has increased and will contribute to the economy for 2017. The destinations chosen for the list were those offering something new or unique for travelers, or places mentioned by experts at Lonely Planet. The authors and editors inspected various destinations around the world before selecting the top 10. Tom Hall, Lonely Planet's Editor-in-Chief, described North Wales as a "lesser-known destination that deserves to be on the world stage". "It's a diverse area with a wealth of activities to draw visitors," he said. "North Wales is ready for its close-up on the global stage." Economy Minister Ken Skates stated that the Northern Wales destination will ensure new tourists for Wales, with a large number of them returning and making a positive contribution to the Welsh economy.

The Church of England and the Church of Scotland, through the Columba Declaration, have committed to strengthening their partnership and growing in communion, with a focus on recognizing each other formally and welcoming clergy and lay people migrating across borders. This move follows the publication of the Growth in Communion, Partnership in Mission report and will be debated by the two Churches' respective synods and assemblies.

The article describes L/Bdr Parkinson, who sustained a serious brain injury in a bomb attack in Afghanistan, and how he has been dramatically touched by the outpouring of support following his participation in the Olympic torch relay, despite Facebook limitations and the sheer volume of requests. Despite this, his mother shares that the family, especially Ben, is thrilled and buoyed by the friend requests, messages of encouragement, and invitations to visit places with the torch.

A large-scale Captagon drug smuggling operation was disrupted at Beirut's airport, with five individuals including a reported Saudi prince being detained and over two tonnes of pills seized, marking the largest such operation yet at the airport. Captagon, a stimulant pill, has been widely consumed in the Middle East, contributing to conflicts and generating revenue, particularly in the Syrian conflict.

A police inquiry is underway, led by the Sexual Offences, Exploitation and Child Abuse Command, regarding allegations of misconduct at Kids Company, a charity offering support to vulnerable inner-city children. The charity asserts it takes client safety and protection seriously, with regular external reviews of its policies and immediate reporting of any misconduct allegations to the police. Police and NSPCC are asking for anyone with information to come forward.

The Queen, who celebrates her 90th birthday this week, is renowned for her ability to mimic the local brogue of Norfolk and, according to her cousin Margaret Rhodes, possesses a developed sense of humor, especially when things go awry. She can also imitate a Scottish accent due to her time at Balmoral, and a humorous anecdote involves the monarch jokingly commenting on a shopper who mistakenly called her "just like the Queen".

The report by UN-Habitat states that income inequality in Latin America is extremely high, with the richest 20% earning 20 times more than the poorest 20%, and that Guatemala has the widest disparity, while Venezuela shows the most equitable distribution. The survey suggests that by 2050, nearly nine out of 10 Latin Americans will live in cities, and the report recommends these nations to use the current period of economic stability and slower population growth to make urban life more equitable, addressing issues such as high unemployment, large labor informality, and combating income disparities.

A Carmarthenshire councillor Tegwen Devichand, who is Labour deputy group leader at Carmarthenshire council, is facing criticism for apparently sharing a far-right group's post on Facebook that supports the death penalty for sex predators. She allegedly shared the post by Britain First, though she denied remembering sharing it and opposes the death penalty. Devichand has been controversial for opposing plans to remove English-stream education at Ysgol Llangennech, a decision that was approved by Carmarthenshire council in January. The decision has been controversial within the council, with one Labour councillor describing it as "segregation... at worst, apartheid." Additionally, Plaid Cymru has accused Labour members of working with UKIP to undermine the council's decision. There are ongoing investigations regarding the matter within the Labour party.

The Iraq War Families Campaign Group, led by Relatives of British troops killed in Iraq, launched a crowdfunding campaign to seek justice for the deaths of their loved ones after the Chilcot report. They aim to use funds to hire lawyers to analyze the report, determine if legal action against key persons involved in the 2003 Iraq invasion is viable, and fund a comprehensive opinion approved by expert senior counsel.

Adnan Syed, who is currently serving a life sentence for the 1999 murder of Hae Min Lee, is set to have his case reopened as his defence team presents new evidence, focusing on potential errors in mobile phone records and a possible alibi. A potential witness, Asia McClain, who claims to have seen Syed in a library during the suspected killing, was not presented in the original trial. The reopening of the case is due to apparent errors and possible new evidence, some of which were discovered in the Serial podcast.

A 16-year-old boy was found guilty of assaulting a taxi driver with a machete after the four boys left a party in Dundee, Scotland. His sentence was deferred for a month due to unfinished social work background reports and his previous custodial sentences for assaults committed at age 14 and 15. One of his friends also admitted to theft during the incident.

In a close and hard-fought ballot, John Clancy, a long-time Labour councillor for Quinton, was chosen as the new leader of Birmingham City Council, defeating several rivals by a single vote. Clancy, who has previously sought the position multiple times, replaces Sir Albert Bore on December 1st. As leader, he plans to improve social housing, provide free school meals, and focus on smarter financial decision-making, while critics within his party have expressed concerns about his ability to achieve the massive and rapid improvements needed to keep off government commissioners. The council, which has faced scrutiny from a government-appointed panel, has been under investigation following revelations from the so-called Trojan Horse letter.

The interview in the June edition of Empire magazine featured Moore discussing his early meetings with Bond film director Guy Hamilton, where they aimed to avoid any deliberate comparisons to Sean Connery while playing the same character. The conversation took place ahead of Skyfall's release, which stars Daniel Craig as 077 and is directed by Sam Mendes. Barbara Broccoli, the film's producer, noted how Connery broke traditional leading man stereotypes in the Bond series and emphasized the vision of her father Cubby Broccoli and Harry Saltzman in ignoring the typical class structure, creating an authentic and unconventional character from Sean Connery. The article also highlights the roles of "unsung heroes" like Yat Malmgren, a Swedish dance teacher that helped Connery improve his movement and gestures, and Dr No scriptwriter Terence Young who introduced Connery to his Savile Row tailors and had him sleep in the suits to establish the character's sophisticated yet functional appearance.

"Witches' marks", historically carved for protection against witchcraft and evil spirits, are being encouraged to be documented this Halloween by Historic England due to their common presence in medieval and Tudor buildings, with the "Daisy Wheel" and Mary-related symbols most prevalent.

The article describes a humorously contentious exchange between Prime Minister Theresa May, Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, and actor Sir Tony Robinson during Prime Minister's Questions, in which Corbyn compared May's Brexit strategy to Baldrick's inscrutable "cunning plans" from the TV show Blackadder, and Robinson agreed, while also mocking May's famous phrase "Brexit means Brexit."

The Liverpool County Court ruled against Jet2 and three other UK airlines who were seeking to delay flight compensation payments, stating that justice is better served promptly, and encouraging thousands of similar passengers to claim their due under EU regulations.

Jamie Dimon, CEO of JP Morgan, has stated that the number of jobs moving out of the UK to EU cities like Dublin and Frankfurt is no longer in the UK's control, as the EU has the power to dictate more job relocations from London to the EU over time. French Prime Minister Edouard Philippe, at the same event, promised incentives like lower taxes, easier hiring and firing, English law courts, and English-speaking schools to attract bankers to Paris, with HSBC CEO Stuart Gulliver expressing interest in the proposed reforms despite some reservations.

China has deployed surface-to-air missiles on a disputed island in the South China Sea, which is claimed by multiple countries and a significant global shipping route. China defends these actions as self-defense within international law, but regional leaders, including the US, have expressed concern about escalating tensions and the potential militarization of the region.

Scientists found that Adanson's house spiders use their silk draglines to stabilize their bodies in mid-air and brake, allowing them to land poised to catch prey. This discovery could inspire the design of small, maneuverable robots.

The Supreme Court has ruled that the UK government is not legally obliged to consult devolved assemblies, including in Wales, on Brexit, but the Welsh Government is expecting the UK government to uphold the Sewel Convention, which grants the assembly a say, and there may be a vote in the Welsh Assembly regarding the triggering process, although it does not carry a veto power.

The Co-op Bank, renowned for its ethical stance and with four million customers, is on the verge of finalizing a plan for recapitalization with existing investors, having earlier sought to meet Bank of England regulations by putting itself on the market. The negotiations also involve the potential separation of the bank's pension fund from the Co-operative Group's scheme due to the unattractiveness of the current arrangement, which entails the bank carrying a share of the Group's £8bn pension liabilities. The bank has reported multiple annual losses, including a deficit of £477m in 2016, an improvement from the £610m loss in 2015.

The Swansea tidal lagoon project, estimated by NRW to potentially kill 21% of salmon and 25% of sea trout each year, has been disputed by Tidal Lagoon Power (TLP) who claim the figures lack a "clear scientific basis" and that their own modeling suggests a "worst case scenario" of 2% of all fish species dying. TLP views the project as a test bed for future, larger and more cost-effective lagoons. UK government ministers are considering a six-month review of the scheme's viability, while both the Welsh Government and industry await clarity on the UK government's position in the near future. NRW stands by its evidence and methodology, stating they have shared it extensively with TLP.

Despite limiting recruitment from non-EU countries, the government's immigration cap has been criticized for being counter-productive as it has increased net migration, particularly in the case of nurses from the EU, potentially causing a crisis in the NHS.

Twenty-year-old off-duty soldier Matthew Boyd was brutally attacked and killed outside a bar in Brecon by Jake Vallely, who claimed to be the "hardest man in Brecon" during a seven-hour drinking binge. Vallely's friend Aaeron Evans was cleared of any involvement in the attack, as the jury determined he was not present during the attack. The trial was described as shocking by the police, and the solider's family expressed their grief, calling Vallely's actions despicable and leaving a void in their family that will never be filled. Vallely will be sentenced on December 8th.

The BBC, in collaboration with tech company This Place, is trialing a brainwave-reading headset that allows users to control BBC's iPlayer, opening up the possibility of people with disabilities operating TVs using their mind, following similar trials with drone control.

The Chief Inspector of Schools, Meilyr Rowlands, and Strategic Director for Estyn, Claire Morgan, testified that the focus on certain performance indicators in schools has led to a focus on borderline grades, leaving more able learners' progress stifled. Ministers have agreed to make changes to raise standards and provide more support for gifted students, introducing measures such as the Seren Network and revising school performance evaluation systems.

An forthcoming posthumous Johnny Cash album titled Out Among the Stars, featuring previously unheard recordings from 1981 and 1984 with duets with June Carter Cash and Waylon Jennings, is set to release in March. It signifies another work of art from the iconic singer who sold over 90 million records, with this release expected to continue the lucrative business for the Cash estate. The estate maintains that releasing these unreleased recordings would be worthy, similar to exhibiting an unseen Picasso, as it would bring more of Cash's music to fans, serving the underprivileged and those who resonate with his music.

The tribunal ruled that Maria McKeith was unfairly dismissed from the Ardoyne Association due to her role as primary carer for her disabled daughter, violating the Disability Discrimination Act 1995. The tribunal awarded her compensation for injury to feelings, loss of earnings, and interest. The Court of Appeal dismissed the Ardoyne Association's appeal. Dr Michael Wardlow, Chief Commissioner of the Equality Commission, emphasized the importance of employers being aware of their responsibilities to avoid discriminating against disabled individuals and their primary caregivers.

Scottish midfielder and former Norwich City player, Glasgow Rangers signed Scottish international Graham Dorrans after two unsuccessful bids by Ibrox club for him were rejected by Norwich City. Dorrans, excited about his move, signed a three-year deal, expressing his long-held desire to play for Rangers. He has previously had a notable career, including seven years at West Bromwich Albion, following his senior debut for Livingston.

Scotland's teams, skipped by siblings Eve and Thomas Brewster, achieved victories in Perth's Dewars Centre, securing men's and women's spots for the European Championships. Eve, thrilled about the home event, highlighted the advantage of competing in her native country. Thomas noted a strong start against stiff competition, while his girlfriend Anna Sloan is anticipated to make her return from injury at the upcoming tournament.

Councillor Pierre Oxley accused the council of being unclear about the sand-to-shingle ratio in a beach recharge project, and called for a scrutiny meeting on Tuesday, which Peter Halliday, in response, called a form of "scaremongering". The meeting will be held to discuss resident concerns about the composition of the beach, particularly its playability, while the council maintains they have been transparent throughout the process.

John Nelms, co-owner of Dundee Football Club, announced plans to submit a land use application for property in Camperdown Park, aiming to improve the club, as they grapple with financial losses, rising stadium maintenance costs, and stadium infrastructure issues.

In the Criterium du Dauphine, Spain's Jesus Herrada won stage two by two seconds over Tony Gallopin, while overall leader Alberto Contador maintained his six-second lead over Richie Porte. Chris Froome, two-time Tour de France winner, is 13 seconds behind Contador in third place. Froome will not compete in the British Championships due to focus on the Tour de France and Olympic Games.

Ex-EastEnders star Sian Blake and her two sons, Zachary and Amon, were found dead at their home with head and neck injuries. The police are seeking her partner, Arthur Simpson-Kent, who is believed to have fled to Ghana. The deaths are being treated as a triple murder. The Met police, who are conducting the investigation, have referred their handling of the case to the IPCC for a thorough investigation into their response to concerns about the family's welfare. Sian Blake played Frankie Pierre in the BBC One soap between 1996 and 1997.

Due to ongoing matches that could not be completed, Wimbledon organizers are scheduled to start play on all courts (including Centre and Court One) at 11:30 BST on Sunday, marking the fourth time in Wimbledon history that there has been play on the middle Sunday. This decision is aimed at avoiding sections of the draw from getting too far apart, which would have resulted in women's matches progressing into the weekdays, potentially causing schedule conflicts with good weather conditions.

Despite initially agreeing to lead Sunderland temporarily, Dick Advocaat decided to stay on and save them from relegation last season. However, he is now leaving the club after only eight games this season, having failed to secure a win, breaking the trend of managers joining to save the club from the drop and leaving in the next season. His departure follows his previous promise to his wife and the club's poor performance this season. Assistant head coach Zeljko Petrovic has also left.

Russia's economy, already struggling due to energy exports decline and Western sanctions, is predicted to experience a 0.8% GDP decline next year, following a 0.6% GDP growth in 2014, and the rouble has lost about half its value against the dollar in 2015, prompting the government to take measures to secure banks and stabilize the economy, such as doubling deposit guarantees and providing direct loans to Sberbank.

Following his defeat in the Kenyan presidential election, opposition leader Mr. Odinga has accused the electoral authorities of fraud and is taking the case to the Supreme Court, claiming widespread irregularities and a lack of fairness. His decision to seek legal redress doesn't signal surrender, but rather a fight for the rights of voters who participated in the election. However, his calls for protests were largely ignored on Monday. In 2013, Odinga also challenges the election results in the Supreme Court without success, presenting an opportunity for the court to demonstrate its independence and address the current allegations of fraud.

A 60-year-old scuba diver on a tour at Agincourt Reef in Far North Queensland was found in distress, revived but could not be revived, marking another tragic incident following two French tourists' deaths due to cardiac arrests while snorkeling at Michaelmas Cay on Wednesday.

The UK and Scottish governments, along with Dundee City Council, have agreed a 3.7 million pound public service obligation (PSO) contract to continue Loganair's operation of the Dundee-London Stansted route for another two years, providing two weekday return flights and one return flight on Sundays. This move aims to maintain connectivity, support trade and tourism in Scotland, and potentially attract additional routes.

WWE is set to launch its video streaming service in mainland China via its partner PPTV, marking the first time a dedicated WWE channel will be available, and is aiming to tap into the large Chinese market, with the success of local stars being critical to its success.

Three men, including a West Midlands police officer, are being questioned on suspicions of providing false information about a supposed kidnap plot involving a colleague and conspiracy to pervert the course of justice, following a hoax tip-off that prompted the police force to issue an alert and instigate heightened precautions in December, when the national threat level was severe.

Ireland secured victory in a must-win game, leading 4-1 against Poland, with key contributions from McKee, Magee, and O'Donoghue. Ireland coach Craig Fulton praised his team's performance, commenting on their improved play and areas for further development. The winners will face Wales in the semi-final, with both teams aiming for a spot in the final and World League 3. France and Scotland will compete in the other semi-final at the same venue.

A 38-year-old man named Philip Craig was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum of 25 years for the murder of 24-year-old Christopher Laskaris, who had Asperger's Syndrome and bi-polar disorder, in Leeds, UK. Craig exploited Laskaris, supplying him with drugs, and left him dead or dying, later stealing items from his flat and selling them. The family of Laskaris expressed their relief at the conviction but acknowledged that nothing could heal their loss. A second man, Dempsey Pattison, who was also charged with the murder was discharged in February.

The Metropolitan Police has closed the reinvestigation of Kester David's 2010 death under a bridge, apologizing to his family for earlier failures and insensitivity in the initial investigation, while also stating that there is no evidence or information indicating a third party was involved in his death.

In 2015, football had the highest overall attendance of 43.4 million, followed by three horse racing events among the top 10 attended events. Rugby union attendances increased to 7.5 million due to the Rugby World Cup. Wimbledon again topped the individual events attendance list, with Formula 1's British Grand Prix being the most attended per-event-day. Two new events, MotoGP's British Grand Prix and the Badminton Horse Trials, entered the top 10, replacing the Ryder Cup and Aintree Grand National. Despite falling short of the record 75 million set in 2012, overall attendances rose by 6% in 2015, excluding one-off effects of the Olympic and Paralympic Games and the Rugby World Cup.

Beyoncé topped the Forbes list for the highest-earning musician of 2013-2014, accumulating an estimated $105 million, largely due to her record-breaking "Mrs. Carter World Tour," lucrative endorsements, and a surprise album release. Taylor Swift came in second with $64 million, followed by Pink with $52 million. The list also included Rihanna and Katy Perry with earnings of $48 million and $40 million, respectively. The ranking was determined by examining income from tours, record sales, publishing, merchandise, endorsements, and other ventures.

The Scottish National Party argues that it has more support among MPs than Labour, with 54 SNP MPs compared to 40 expressing support for Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, but Speaker John Bercow maintains that Labour remains the official opposition due to parliamentary rules, despite challenges to Corbyn's leadership.
