Despite pressure from the US government to extradite him for espionage charges, Russian President Vladimir Putin has stated that Snowden could stay in Russia if he stops leaking US secrets. Snowden is reportedly anxious about leaving, and is interested in studying Russian culture. The diplomatic and political implications of Snowden's case are causing ructions around the world, with some countries, including Bolivia, Venezuela, and Nicaragua, offering him asylum.

Brazil's Attorney-General, Rodrigo Janot, has petitioned the Supreme Court to investigate former President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who served from 2003 to 2011, for his alleged involvement in the Operation Car Wash scandal involving kickbacks at state-oil company Petrobras. The specific charges and evidence against Lula remain undisclosed, but his link to the scandal allegedly comes from illegitimate benefits, such as renovations of a luxury apartment and ranch for his family, resulting from the Petrobras corruption scheme. Lula, a political mentor of President Dilma Rousseff, was questioned by police and has denied any wrongdoing. If Lula were to be charged, this could significantly increase pressure on Rousseff, who is currently facing impeachment proceedings.

The government has rejected calls to remove its immunity from prosecution under the 2007 Corporate Manslaughter Act, following the deaths of three SAS candidates in a selection march in 2013 due to hyperthermia. The bereaved family believes holding the Ministry of Defence legally accountable would improve training safety, while the government argues that existing mechanisms are sufficient to learn from mistakes and prevent future fatalities.

The defending Premier League champions, Leicester City, are struggling in the league, having lost to League One side Millwall in the FA Cup, and are currently one point above the relegation zone, with manager Claudio Ranieri expressing disappointment in the team's lackluster performance and calling for more determination and fight from the players.

The article discusses that hundreds of millions of pounds from image rights of footballers and entertainers are allegedly being paid into offshore accounts without tax deducted, leading to HMRC conducting multiple investigations into potential irregularities in tax affairs, with 43 players, eight agents, and 12 football clubs being under investigation, yielding £158m in the last two years.

The controversial treason investigation into two German journalists for publishing classified documents, revealing plans to expand online surveillance in Germany, has been halted after national outrage and public protests, resulting in the government's unprecedented firing of the chief prosecutor. The case has sparked a national debate on freedom of the press, government influence over the courts, and the definition of a journalist in the digital age, raising more questions about what constitutes a state secret and what can be published.

The article discusses George Osborne's Budget speech that lacked significant measures for the South East region, despite it being a key Conservative stronghold in the upcoming election, with a focus on stimulating growth in regions like the North West and Yorkshire instead.

Despite Doncaster Rovers' struggles to break through an intense Colchester United midfield pressure, they managed to take a 1-0 lead into half-time thanks to a goal by Rowe, with Marquis missing several opportunities to extend the lead in the second half. Colchester had the more dangerous chances but couldn't find the back of the net, and Doncaster held on for the win.

Ross McEwan, the CEO of Royal Bank of Scotland (RBS), told BBC Newsnight that uncertainty caused by the EU vote could "slow down banking," and he urged for the referendum to be held as early as possible, ideally in June. He also mentioned that he expects no interest rate rise before 2017, and although RBS has posted consecutive years of losses, it has set aside funds to cover fines for mis-selling and PPI payments. He expressed that the likelihood of British taxpayers getting the £45bn invested in RBS back is remote.

At the 2015 general election, the Scottish National Party (SNP) focuses on Scottish independence and progressive policies, while Labour aims to build up the UK and emphasizes principled reasons for not striking deals with the SNP. The Liberal Democrats promise to boost mental health services and claim they will hold the center ground on political issues, avoiding extreme influences like UKIP's Nigel Farage. The Conservatives emphasize the importance of keeping Scotland's economy strong and maintaining its place in the UK.

A physics student, Elliot Vale, along with his girlfriend Tia Mountain, developed GeoRescue, an app that provides information on natural disasters and guides people to safety, using GPS for rescue service location. They are presenting this concept at a space conference, planning to pitch it to a panel of space experts for potential development into a real app. The app would highlight disaster-prone areas and offer a distress beacon to call for help.

Sir Timothy O'Shea, a university leader, expresses concerns about proposed changes in the Scottish government's Higher Education Governance Bill, arguing that the plan for directly elected chairs of university governing bodies could be damaging, particularly to the role of the rector at ancient universities, and may impede the university's ability to contribute to the country's economic and social good. The government, however, maintains that the bill aims to give a say to the entire campus community in university governance and will continue to listen to stakeholders' views.

The article describes Elena Hrabovenska, a Ukrainian woman who runs a Polish deli in Huntingdon, facing hate speech and potential threats after the Brexit vote. Despite difficulties, she sees potential for integration and assimilation among the new generation and predicts her shop, among others, will eventually blend into the English community.

An anonymous threat led to heightened security measures, a search for a suspicious person, and the deployment of SWAT officers at the Dallas Police Department headquarters two days after a black man shot and killed five police officers in retaliation for police killings of black men, following a protest rally against police killings of black men.

The article discusses calls from within Australia's political parties and states for increased support for Syrian and Iraqi refugees, with some proposing temporary housing and additional refugee places, while the Prime Minister has pledged to increase Syrian asylum seekers but stopped short of boosting overall refugee numbers.

Nigel Farage, UKIP leader, claims the target to reduce UK's net migration cannot be achieved while the country remains in the EU, and criticizes other parties for making false promises about immigration during the election campaign. His party's immigration policy remains central to their campaign, but critics have accused UKIP of policy chaos. The EU, and the UK's place within it, is set to be a major issue in the election campaign.

Gareth Southgate, a former England defender and ex-Middlesbrough boss, has been appointed as the permanent England manager. He has demonstrated a winning mentality and strong understanding of international football, according to the Football Association. Southgate will lead England in their upcoming friendly against Germany on 22 March, marking his first competitive match in charge. His previous managerial experience includes a 151-game stint with Middlesbrough, during which he presided over their relegation from the Premier League.

The FBI has ordered Apple to disable security software on a murderer's iPhone, but the tech company has declined. Notably, Mark Zuckerberg, Amazon, Google, and Twitter leaders support Apple's stance while a representative for victims sympathizes with the FBI's goal but opposes the proposed method. The debate between privacy and national security continues.

The article discusses various events and tributes marking the Queen's 90th birthday, including pronouncements from the Prince of Wales and Prince William stating that the Queen has been a guiding example of a good monarch, tributes from political leaders, and the release of special stamps in her honor. Critics have questioned Prince William's commitment to royal duty in the media, but he has stated that he takes his responsibilities seriously and will continue to do so when the time comes to accept more responsibility.

Star Trek Beyond has incorporated a gay character into its universe, with Sulu being revealed as homosexual and having a male partner. This decision has been met with varying opinions from cast members, with George Takei expressing disapproval due to his belief that creator Gene Roddenberry intended Sulu to be heterosexual, while others, including Zachary Quinto, support the move for representation. The release of the film coincides with the 50th anniversary of Star Trek and carries dedications to the late Anton Yelchin and Leonard Nimoy.

Peterborough United started strongly against Bristol Rovers, scoring three goals in the first half through Marriott, Taylor, and a consolation goal by Rory Gaffney. Marriott scored two more in the second half, finishing with a hat-trick. Rovers managed a consolation goal through Gaffney again, but struggled to create a considerable number of chances.

IS jihadists attempted to seize the ancient city of Palmyra, a UNESCO World Heritage site, on Thursday, but their advance was reportedly halted by the Syrian army. The Syrian antiquities chief has warned that if IS takes control, it will destroy the site, as they have already ransacked and demolished several ancient sites in Iraq. The city is strategically important and has already suffered damage due to the Syrian civil war. If IS were to capture Palmyra, it would likely be an "international catastrophe," as it would trigger a repetition of the destruction seen in other ancient sites in Iraq.

A medical researcher and other passengers on a high-speed train from Amsterdam to Paris were abandoned by staff who ran and locked themselves away in a service room during a gun attack, subsequently expressing remorse and questioning the staff's actions. The drama unfolded on Friday, with passengers locked in a compartment for ten minutes until a man entered and assured them the situation was under control, later identified as one of the American passengers who helped overpower the attacker.

GB Taekwondo's decision to nominate Muhammad (ranked 59th in the world) over the world number one Cook has been upheld by the BOA, despite criticism for a lack of transparency and impact on both athletes. Cook's camp is considering legal action, as they believe his exclusion from the London Olympics is an absolute disgrace, given his world number one ranking, European championship, and strong performance against top athletes. The BOA notes the importance of closer collaboration with national governing bodies regarding selection policies for future Games.

British tourists Hannah Witheridge and David Miller were found dead on a beach on Koh Tao island, and their case initially implicated the Ware brothers from Jersey. However, forensic tests revealed DNA traces of two men from neither the Ware brothers nor the 11 Burmese suspects questioned. The police investigation has made little progress, admitting they don't know where to look now, and have now allowed the Ware brothers to leave Thailand. The case follows a pattern in investigating murders of British citizens in Thailand, where foreigners or immigrants are often initially considered main suspects. The prime minister has apologized for a controversial comment he made suggesting attractive women in bikinis could not be safe.

Japan is committing to increasing the popularity of rugby union, particularly in the lead-up to the 2019 World Cup, by promoting the sport in schools, local government-funded stadiums, and through a focus on raising awareness and interest among the general populace. The goal is to create a wider audience for live rugby games in Japan, following a successful model seen in the 2002 World Cup and the upcoming 2020 Tokyo Olympics.

The article suggests that the "supply-side" of revolutions is often overlooked, highlighting that the role of the army in controlling and guiding political transitions is crucial. Independent, professional armies can enable peaceful transitions, while armies that are closely tied to autocratic regimes tend to use force against protesters, potentially leading to civil war or prolonged conflict. The piece emphasizes the importance of understanding the dynamics between civil and military forces in determining the trajectory of an uprising, and the role outside actors play in capacity-building for both regime forces and rebelling groups.

The unemployment rate in the UK fell to its lowest level since 2005, with 1.68 million people out of work and average weekly earnings growing by 2%, the slowest increase since February. The jobless rate has not triggered excessive pay growth, and it is considered that the first post-crisis rate hike may be pushed back into 2017. The employment rate hit 74%, and almost 23 million people are now in a full-time job, with the economic inactivity rate for women reaching a record low of 27%.

Middlesbrough scored two goals against Bournemouth for the first time this season, with Ramirez and Downing each scoring for the first time this term, resulting in a 2-0 win for Middlesbrough, despite the efforts of striker Alvaro Negredo being below par. Bournemouth struggled with intensity levels after a promising start.

Two Williams drivers, Felipe Massa and Valtteri Bottas, sustained left-rear wheel failures, while Renault's Kevin Magnussen is suspected to have a broken left rear suspension. These issues caused a track investigation and delay in the Chinese Grand Prix first practice session. Mercedes driver Nico Rosberg topped the session's times, while Lewis Hamilton had an ignition problem. Sebastian Vettel was third, followed by Daniel Ricciardo, Kimi Raikkonen, Daniil Kvyat, Carlos Sainz, Jenson Button, and Fernando Alonso, who returned after missing the last race due to a broken rib. Alonso faced further medical checks to determine his ability to continue in the rest of the weekend.

Hibs thrashed Bonnyrigg Rose in a one-sided Scottish Cup tie, with Andrew Shinnie, James Keatings, Chris Humphrey, Jason Cummings (twice), Lewis Stevenson, and Jordon Forster scoring for Hibs, while Dean Hoskins converted a penalty for Bonnyrigg Rose.

The Ugandan president is facing criticism for a letter to parliament criticizing its speaker for passing a bill that criminalizes homosexual acts, promoting homosexuality, and failing to report gay people without a quorum, and for calling homosexuals "abnormal" or "sick." The bill, which also adds female-to-female sex to banned practices, has been condemned by world leaders since it was first mooted in 2009 and could see some countries suspend aid to the country if signed into law. The government is trying to persuade MPs to reject the bill, but some have already said they would go against their government's wishes.

Manager Neil Slade and his Cardiff team are one point away from the Premier League, a feat that would be the pinnacle of his career. Despite prior play-off experiences with lower-division teams (Grimsby, Yeovil, and Leyton Orient) not resulting in promotion, these campaigns remain a highlight for him. In the coming match against Reading, key players David Marshall, Fabio, and Peter Whittingham are questionable due to illness and injury.

The article discusses Scotland's current qualification run in the women's Euro tournament, with their upcoming match against Iceland being crucial to secure their place. Bayern Munich forward Evans, who plays in a top league, emphasizes the potential emotional impact if they make it to the finals after previous play-off losses. Iceland, also undefeated, tops the group, and the upcoming matches could determine the group leader. Evans highlights the benefits of playing in top leagues for the national team, improving their chances of qualification.

Claire, a former event-rider, is using a robotic walking suit to participate in the London Marathon, aiming to prove her resilience despite being paralysed from the chest down after a horse-riding accident in 2006. She hopes to improve her speed and walk a mile in one session, even though it takes over two hours, and aims to raise funds for Spinal Research.

Jack Walsh, a 23-year-old from Lisburn, is currently working for the YouTube gaming channel Game Grumps in Los Angeles, where he shoots and directs commercials and assists in expanding the company's content into TV comedy on YouTube's Red channel. His passion for filmmaking was sparked in high school and led him to study in film school, where he got the opportunity to work with renowned composer John Debney, resulting in him writing and directing his own short film musical. Despite the growing film industry in Northern Ireland, Walsh is not yet ready to return home as he hopes to advance further in his career in Los Angeles.

The first minister of Scotland, Nicola Sturgeon, has been recognized as one of the world's most powerful and influential women by Forbes magazine, with her 50th overall ranking underscoring the significance of her office and Scotland's status as a nation. The list is based on factors such as influence, media presence, wealth, and success at implementing change, with German Chancellor Angela Merkel topping the list for the 6th consecutive year. Other notable figures include Hillary Clinton, Janet Yellen, Melinda Gates, and Mary Barra.

The article presents a study by an international team of scientists, which discovered that several species, including reindeers, have ultra-violet sensitivity in their vision. This UV sensitivity might cause them to avoid electrical power lines due to the UV emission from the power line's corona, which could disrupt animal habitats and migration patterns. The researchers emphasized that the random and unpredictable nature of the corona's flashes could make it problematic for animals to adapt to and avoid.

A former Kids Company employee told BBC Two's Newsnight that allegations of sexual exploitation by clients towards other clients were raised with the charity at an Urban Academy in Southwark, South-East London, but were not passed on to authorities. Kate, a former client of the charity, claimed she was inappropriately touched over a seven-month period in 2009, and when she attempted to tell a teacher, the conversation was stopped before she could explain the sexual assault allegations. Ella, a former paid employee, alleged she was the victim of a sexual assault by a co-worker in 2009, but the accused was never suspended or adequately dealt with by the charity. Despite the charity's Chairman, Alan Yentob, claiming no evidence of sexual abuse was presented to them, Camila Batmanghelidjh, the charity's founder, said she would have reacted by reporting the incident to the police.

A Brexit voter, Paul Austin, has expressed concerns about immigration, taxation, and potential quality control issues in imported goods following recent events and the Grenfell Tower fire, causing him to question his initial stance on Brexit.

England, who were initially on the verge of a draw, had a dramatic comeback win over Pakistan in the first Test owing to debutant Adil Rashid's five-wicket haul, after Pakistan were cruising at 113-3, but eventually ended up losing due to fading light, finishing 25 runs short of the victory target, with the score reading 74-4. Despite mistakes earlier in the match and several wickets lost later on, England performed exceptionally well overall, with Cook's record-breaking 263 in the first innings laying the foundation for their impressive total of 598-9, and a promising bowling performance from Stokes, Anderson, and Rashid. The second Test match in Dubai is set to begin on Thursday.

Celtic manager Brendan Rodgers was pleased with French midfielder Oliver Ntcham's performance in a friendly game, noting his impressive range of passing and potential to play at top level. He also praised 19-year-old Kundai Benyu, who impressed with his technical skills, mobility, and competitive edge, and has earned a longer stay with the team. The match, won by Lyon 4-0, provided valuable fitness time for Celtic players, despite a drop in quality during the second half.

A vaccine produced by GlaxoSmithKline and the US National Institutes of Health, aimed at preventing Ebola, is expected to be shipped to Liberia with plans for trials on 30,000 volunteers. The vaccine will be compared against a placebo, with 10,000 volunteers receiving the GSK vaccine and another 10,000 a separate experimental jab. Experts suggest that the declining Ebola case numbers may make it challenging to establish the vaccine's efficacy.

The Blackpool versus Wycombe Wanderers football match ended scoreless despite multiple attempts missed by both teams, with key moments including Taylor, Harriman, Potts, Akinfenwa, McAlister, and Cullen having promising shots, and with several corners and free kicks taken by both teams throughout the game.

The Australian government offered a A$70 million settlement to more than 1,900 asylum seekers who claimed they suffered harm while held on PNG's Manus Island between 2012 and 2016. The settlement was deemed a "prudent" decision by the government, despite ongoing criticism of Australia's offshore refugee processing policy. The government maintains no-one held on Manus or Nauru will ever be resettled in Australia.

Former England midfielder Paul Scholes, 37, who spent his entire career at Manchester United, has returned to the club as a player due to an injury crisis in midfield and helped United secure a 3-2 win at Manchester City with a 31-minute cameo. Scholes, who had retired at the end of last season, spent 19 years at Old Trafford, winning 10 Premier League titles and 2 Champions League trophies.

A Welsh animator, who created the much-loved character SuperTed to comfort his stepson's fear of the dark, later started a successful animation company in Hollywood, and is now planning a new series of SuperTed in Wales, while also working on a film about a legendary Cardiff City football player, Robin Friday.

The far-right movement has been reshaping Europe's political landscape, with various nationalist parties making significant gains in different countries. In Austria, the Freedom Party (FPOe) has gained significant influence with Norbert Hofer's election as president. Greece's Golden Dawn, considered neo-Nazi by many, has gained representation in the parliament. In Denmark, the Danish People's Party (DPP) has played a crucial role in shaping the country's immigration policy. Similar trends are seen in Finland, France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, the Netherlands, and Slovakia, where nationalist parties are pushing for strict immigration controls and challenging the traditional political establishment.

Tottenham chairman Daniel Levy defended their lack of summer signings and emphasized the club's spending is geared towards sustainability, while manager Antonio Conte believes the team's expectations should be tempered given their current status. Chelsea, who have spent about £130m on three new players, are reportedly interested in Spurs' striker Harry Kane but he would come at a hefty price, according to Conte.

The article discusses a significant increase in arrests of disruptive, drunken passengers at UK airports from 2015 to 2016, with more than half of surveyed cabin crew reporting incidents. The Home Office is considering implementing tougher rules on alcohol, and trade body Airlines UK is advocating for a ban on passengers drinking their own alcohol on planes. However, a voluntary industry code of conduct has been introduced but is often ignored and viewed as ineffective by cabin crew. Lobby groups are suggesting stronger regulations, including revoking airports' exemption from the Licensing Act.

Silverstone, the host of the British Grand Prix since 1987, has announced it may not be able to continue hosting the event after 2019 due to financial losses, as the contract requires a £12m fee that has escalated over the years. However, the event's future is not confirmed, with F1's new chairman expressing interest in other UK locations, such as a potential London street race. Nonetheless, many, including former world champion Nigel Mansell, believe it would be unfortunate if historic Silverstone no longer hosted grand prix racing.

In the Premier League game between Hull City and Manchester United, Marcus Rashford scored a late winner to secure a 1-0 victory for the Red Devils, after they had gone close through Rooney, Ibrahimovic, and Pogba; the match marked Rashford's first appearance of the season. United and Chelsea are the only teams with a 100% record from three games, while Manchester City will aim to keep pace when they play West Ham on Sunday. Hull, who had six points from nine in their first three games, suffered their first defeat of the season, with Ryan Mason being a potential future signing for the club.

Ben Stokes, the England all-rounder who was suspended from the 2014 World Twenty20 for punching a locker, expresses his intention to maintain his competitive spirit while acknowledging the need for occasional self-restraint. He recently became the most expensive foreign player in the Indian Premier League and returned to action in a series against West Indies, known for their powerful batsmen and fast bowlers. England, who have won nine of their past 10 ODIs against West Indies, are aiming for another victory, but the West Indies, though inexperienced due to selection changes, are still expected to present a tough challenge.

Coventry City College is attempting to help students who failed to obtain C grades in English and Maths GCSEs at school, by employing new teachers and retraining existing staff to teach these subjects. The aim is to enable students to achieve C grades, which are essential for many apprenticeships and vocational courses, as these skills are considered crucial for career progression. Success stories include Reece Beal in coach-making and Samantha Richards in hairdressing, who struggled with these subjects at school but are now thriving.

The article discusses a letter sent by Mr. Skates accusing Network Rail of insufficient investment in clearing leaves this autumn, causing increased damage to train wheels, overcrowding, and reduced punctuality of services. Network Rail denies this and is committed to working together with the Welsh Government to ensure value for taxpayers' money. Additionally, the poor conditions of trains in Wales are described as a "national crisis" by Adam Price in a Senedd debate, with examples of fires, overcrowding, and a passenger not having a seat for 11 months.

The session involved discussions on various topics including Brexit, devolution, steel, and the Severn crossings; Alun Cairns, UK Secretary of State for Wales, noted potential advantages in Brexit are wider market opportunities and focusing on international trade, he also mentioned no changes planned to Wales Bill but intends to have a fiscal framework agreed with Welsh Government before it becomes law, and there are no plans to change the Barnett Formula.

In the English T20 Blast, Hampshire secured a surprising victory against Leicestershire by 24 runs under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern system, with Paul Collingwood (34) and Paul Coughlin (38 not out) being key contributors after a 63-run blitz by Luke Ronchi for Leicestershire. Meanwhile, several other matches were postponed due to heavy rain, with Sussex versus Middlesex ending in an abandonment. Despite this victory, Durham remains at the bottom of the North Group, and speculation about who will reach the quarter-finals is ongoing.

China, historically the originator of key modern technologies and now home to the world's fastest-growing economy, is undergoing a second industrial revolution. Despite economic reforms and attractive investment opportunities since Mao Zedong's leadership, political reform remains limited, leading to social issues such as corruption, environmental degradation, and human rights concerns, particularly among ethnic minorities like the Uighurs and Tibetans.

The article discusses the intense speculation over who will perform the titular song for the latest James Bond film, Spectre, with betting companies suspending betting on Ellie Goulding after her cryptic Instagram post and a £15,000 bet placed on Radiohead, who are currently the favorites to perform the song. However, neither the band nor the film's makers have confirmed or denied the rumors.

The Scottish government has not planned a referendum for 2017 on Scottish independence, though Nicola Sturgeon has indicated a possible vote could occur if Scotland's view on the European Union is disregarded and a "soft Brexit" is not achieved.

Four individuals, Bakr Hamad, Sharif Kadir, Zana Rahim, and Awat Hamasalih, appeared in court in the UK on Friday and refused consent to extradition. They are alleged to be part of a "jihadist network," Rawti Shax (or "Didi Nwe"), an initiative that is believed to be an evolution of the terrorist organization Ansar al-Islam and aims to establish a caliphate in Iraq's Kurdistan region, with suspected ties to al-Qaeda. Suspected leaders and numerous members of the group were arrested in six European countries, including the UK, as part of a coordinated operation by Eurojust, and the group is reportedly charged with international terrorism. The focus of the investigation appears to have been targeting an international recruiting pipeline that transports jihadists to join the Islamic State and Al-Nusra organizations in Syria and Iraq.

The UK still has a significant way to go in terms of fiscal consolidation, with departmental spending cuts of £51.4bn, or 14.1%, planned for the next parliament, according to the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS). This would mean the lowest share of national income for public spending since at least 1948 and fewer people working in the public sector since at least 1971. Despite less than planned spending cuts so far, the IFS warns that there is still much fiscal work to be done over the next parliament. The green budget also illustrates the central economic choice facing voters in May: bigger cuts with a Tory or Tory-led government, or higher public sector debt with a Labour one. Both parties promise to protect spending on health, education, and overseas aid.

Cambridge United defeated Cheltenham Town 3-1, with Luke Berry scoring a brace for the home side, and Uche Ikpeazu opening the scoring early in the game. A late consolation goal by Billy Waters for Cheltenham Town made the scoreline slightly more respectable.

A controversial bonfire in a public car park at Ravenscroft Avenue in Belfast is the subject of court injunctions, complaints about offensive materials, and investigations into hate crimes for burning flags and election posters. This year's bonfires, traditionally lit to commemorate William of Orange's victory over King James II, have sparked controversy due to their closeness to homes and potential threats to health and safety. Sinn Féin leaders have called for action against the practice, while unionist leaders have defended the bonfires as a part of their culture, urging builders to be respectful of their neighbors. Meanwhile, officials are addressing incidents of racism and distasteful materials on bonfires, and fire crews have dealt with prematurely lit bonfires in several locations.

The article discusses the integration of technology, particularly tablets and smartphones, into television viewing experiences, with companion apps designed to keep viewers engaged during broadcasts, utilizing audio watermarking and other technologies to synchronize content. Examples include apps for The Walking Dead and Sons of Anarchy that allow viewers to predict and track events, with the potential for interactive advertising and other revenue-generating opportunities in the future. The goal is to enhance the viewing experience and maintain audience engagement amidst the increased use of second screens during television consumption.

This article discusses the political pressure on Facebook, Google, and other tech companies to remove hateful content following a terrorist attack by a white man on Muslims. However, it raises concerns about the practical and philosophical challenges of implementing such measures, such as the enormous volume of content, the cross-jurisdictional nature of internet content, and the potential for censorship by private companies with global influence. The author suggests that the consequences of asking tech giants to police the internet more closely should be carefully considered.

The Longford Town Centre, once meant to be a symbol of economic prosperity, now stands as a symbol of Ireland's economic crash. Local traders like Matt O'Brien are seeing a turnaround, but they, along with Fianna Fáil, believe more support and policies are needed to further boost the local economy, such as reducing parking charges and attracting foreign investments through agencies like the Industrial Development Authority. The potential arrival of holiday company Center Parcs in County Longford in 2019 is seen as a positive step, but more is desired to ensure a lasting economic recovery.

The Solar Impulse aircraft, equipped with sun-powered photovoltaic cells and a single pilot, is set to embark on a five to six-day flight from Nanjing, China, to Hawaii, aiming to break aviation records and further demonstrate the potential of clean technologies. The pilot, Bertrand Borschberg, is ready to endure the physically and mentally challenging journey while maintaining continuous communication with his support team in Monaco for meteorological updates and flight strategy advice. Even with the option to return to China or Japan if encountered with unsuitable weather conditions or technical problems, preparations have been made for an emergency Pacific ditching if necessary.

Lord Carey, a former Archbishop of Canterbury, has dropped his opposition to the Assisted Dying Bill, stating that the reality of needless suffering has led him to change his mind. This switch is significant as he now believes it's not "un-Christian" to allow terminally ill individuals to take their own lives when they're suffering. However, the current Archbishop of Canterbury Justin Welby has warned that the bill could put elderly and disabled people under pressure to end their lives. The Assisted Dying Bill, tabled by Labour peer Lord Falconer, would legalize assisted dying for adults with less than six months to live in England and Wales, with two doctors confirming the patient's terminal illness and their informed decision to die. Peers will debate the bill on Friday.

The article discusses reactions to North Korea's alleged H-bomb test, with suggestion for potential solutions including increased international dialogue, UN intervention, imposition of sanctions, and non-aggression, with some advocating for denying North Korea's leader an opportunity to escalate tension and others proposing involvement of figures like Dennis Rodman for further diplomatic efforts.

Refugees and asylum seekers in Belfast, including Mohammed, a former Algerian police officer, find solace and purpose by volunteering for conservation work in the Mourne mountains, where they learn to rebuild dry-stone walls. This initiative, led by the Mourne Heritage Trust and aided by charities like Mediation Northern Ireland, allows refugees to make new friends, improve language skills, and feel a sense of belonging in their new home. The trust also benefits from the volunteers' efforts in repairing damaged walls, with Mohammed being particularly grateful for the peaceful environment the mountains provide.

Stuart Broad's 5-wicket haul in a single spell, aided by challenging conditions, turned the tide against South Africa, who were level at lunch but lost the rest of their wickets in less than two sessions, resulting in a decisive English victory. Broad's performance, characterized by his ability to produce dangerous deliveries and trigger pressure, highlights his match-winning potential. The English team, boasting a number of standout performers, is currently on the rise, having demonstrated a knack for turning games from disadvantageous positions.

The team led by researchers from the British Geological Survey and UCL has produced a continent-wide map detailing the scale and potential of hidden water resources in aquifers beneath Africa, emphasizing the importance of careful exploration and extraction to conserve this vast yet fragile reserve, which they argue could help mitigate the impact of climate change and contribute to meeting future water demands in Africa.

Lord O'Donnell, a former Cabinet Secretary, stated that it would take "years and years and years" for the UK to fully separate from the EU, but there is a possibility that the UK may stay in a loosely-aligned group with the EU, depending on public opinion and changes in the EU. He also noted that Brexit would be a difficult process and that triggering Article 50 should not be rushed, as the government must first prepare a strategic plan.

A 22-year-old woman named Sian O'Callaghan has been missing since she left a nightclub named Suju in Marlborough, UK, at about 0250 GMT on Saturday. A search party comprising of over 400 volunteers, including her friends, boyfriend, and local residents, has been engaged in searching Savernake Forest for her since. An anonymous donor has offered a £20,000 reward for any information leading to her finding. The search will resume at 1030 GMT on Wednesday. Police have stated that her mobile phone was followed into the 4,500-acre forest approximately 32 minutes after she left the club, and the journey could only have been made by car. The search is being treated as a missing person inquiry with over 60 police officers involved. CCTV footage of O'Callaghan alone in the nightclub has been released in hopes of jogging memory for potential witnesses. Her boyfriend Kevin Reape, who shared a flat with O'Callaghan, is not being treated as a suspect in her disappearance.

In the second practice session for the Chinese Grand Prix, Ferrari's Kimi Raikkonen led Mercedes' Valtteri Bottas and Felipe Massa of Williams, with Hamilton, hampered by a five-place grid penalty, lagging in fifth place. Mercedes appears to have an advantage in terms of race pace, but Ferrari's pace in practice may suggest they could challenge McLaren this weekend. However, Ferrari's speed in practice has not translated into strong performances in qualifying this season. Hamilton expressed optimism about the weekend's race, as he anticipates a battle with Ferrari. Other notable performances in practice included Daniel Ricciardo of Red Bull, Max Verstappen of Toro Rosso, and Fernando Alonso of McLaren.

Arlene Foster has pledged to support the campaign for Thalidomide victims seeking compensation from Germany, with Kim Fenton, a local survivor, expressing hope for a breakthrough and potential moral victory in the New Year.

Character actor Eli Wallach, who spanned six decades in a career that began on stage in 1945 and continued into his 90s, was renowned for his versatility and broad range of roles, with his portrayal of the bandit chief Calvera in The Magnificent Seven often considered his definitive role. Throughout his 60-year career, he was unnominated for an Oscar, but received the honorary award in 2011 for his contributions to cinema. Wallach made impactful appearances in various film genres, including westerns, villains in The Good, the Bad and the Ugly, light comedy, and TV shows, with his performance as Mr. Freeze in the 1960s Batman TV series being noteworthy. He also had significant theatre credits, including his 65-year marriage to Anne Jackson, and earned an Emmy for his supporting role in Poppies Are Also Flowers. Wallach passed away in 2016, leaving behind a prolific and enduring body of work.

Hanson Academy implemented a strict school uniform policy on Tuesday, leading to nearly 10% of students being sent home due to non-compliance, causing anger among parents. The school claims it communicated its expectations for the school year clearly. The policy includes rules against hoop earrings, patterned trousers, unnatural hair colors, indoor wear of jackets or coats, and specific types of footwear. Parents express financial and logistical challenges in meeting these requirements, with some stating they cannot afford new shoes or were not timely informed about their children being sent home. The school plans to continue with the policy, promising to help struggling parents.

Violence erupted in Beirut between Sunni pro- and anti-Syrian groups after the killing of two anti-Syrian clerics, marking the first such incident since the conflict in neighboring Syria began. The incident further underscores the deep divisions within Lebanon over the Syrian crisis.

The article discusses Nick Clegg's argument that only a strong coalition involving his party can prevent a second election and save the country from instability, following his party's "two-day dash" campaign, where he suggested the hardening positions of Labour and Conservatives on coalition deals could result in a weak and unstable minority government. Clegg emphasized the Liberal Democrats' role in creating strong and stable coalitions, while warning against a "blue-KIP alliance" or an "Ed Miliband and Alex Salmond deathly embrace" on the left. Clegg refused to comment on private conversations about election outcomes but insisted that the Conservative claim to win a majority by 23 seats is false.

Liverpool suffered a second-half collapse to lose the Europa League final to Sevilla, thus ending their chances of playing any European football next season. Manager Jurgen Klopp apologized for the performance, promising improvement, while former Liverpool defender Mark Lawrenson criticized their defensive errors, particularly left-back Alberto Moreno, who he also blamed for not being strengthened during Brendan Rodgers' tenure. Lawrenson expects significant changes at Anfield this summer, but anticipates strikers Daniel Sturridge, Roberto Firmino, and Philippe Coutinho to remain.

A fatal incident occurred in Sparkbrook, Birmingham, with a man, locally named Ikram Elahi, dead from gunshot or knife wounds. Witnesses claim 200-300 people gathered before the event, and four men were arrested for suspected violent disorder and a fifth for drug possession. The case provoked community concern, and investigations are ongoing.

South African President Jacob Zuma's government is investigating 17 banks, including Barclays, JP Morgan, and HSBC, for suspected collusion to manipulate the foreign exchange market using online chat rooms. If found guilty, the banks could face fines of up to 10% of their in-country annual turnover. The investigation has been welcomed by the government, which sees it as a means to protect the nation's economy, and to establish a state bank. The case comes amid rising political tensions due to allegations of corruption in big business, with some South Africans accusing largely white-owned media of being soft on reporting such corruption.

A special advisor to the economy minister, Mr Robinson, denies any family links to the Renewable Heat Incentive, following allegations made under parliamentary privilege by former enterprise minister MLA Bell, who claimed that two DUP special advisers had "extensive interests in the poultry industry" and influenced the RHI scheme. Meanwhile, both Robinson and fellow DUP special advisor Timothy Johnston deny these claims. The RHI scheme, set up in 2012, was intended to increase renewable heat consumption but led to an overspend of £490m due to businesses receiving more in subsidies than they paid for fuel.

A new technique using CRISPR gene editing, developed by researchers at the University of Washington and Harvard University, allows for the creation of a "molecular tape recorder" that records a permanent mark on a cell's DNA, enabling scientists to trace the lineage and origins of cells in an organism, providing valuable insights into biological development and potentially aiding in the understanding of disease, cancer formation, and inherited diseases.

The man was denied permission to block the Department for the Economy from publishing a list of Renewable Heat Incentive (RHI) recipients, as argued that it could harm his business reputation and cause financial losses. However, the department deemed the potential damage to be minimal and legal. The RHI scheme, intended to promote renewable heat creation, has been oversubscribed, leading to businesses receiving more in subsidies than they pay for renewable fuel. The applicant, who installed a boiler and joined the scheme in 2016, is only eligible for limited payments under cost controls and argues the publication of his details would not differentiate between various tariffs, posing no risk of abuse. The department insists the date of application would be included in the information to be published, allowing the public to distinguish the applicable tariff and verify the scheme's cost controls.

Judge Thokozile Masipa sentenced Oscar Pistorius to five years in prison for culpable homicide in the death of his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp, who was killed on Valentine's Day last year. The defense argued for community service and house arrest, while prosecutors called for a 10-year term. Pistorius's family has stated they will not appeal the sentence. The court case revealed issues with South Africa's gun culture, police, and prisons.

The beach where Tunisia's worst terror attack occurred has reopened, but the emotional scars remain for locals like Sabi, who runs a boat club on the beach and lost several customers in the attack. Tourism, a crucial industry for the nation, is under serious threat as holidaymakers leave on emergency flights, with many staying away due to fear. The Tunisian government is working to reinforce security in response, but the nation continues to grapple with rising Islamist attacks and the impact of neighboring conflict in Libya and Syria.

The article discusses the intentions of British Foreign Secretary Philip Hammond's visit to Tripoli, which is to provide international backing and aid, including £10m, to the newly established Government of National Accord in Libya, as instability in Libya is creating ungoverned spaces where IS is taking root, causing problems for Europe, like the refugee crisis and trafficking. The visit aims to offer practical assistance, such as counter-terrorism and tackling illegal migration, but the extent and military dimension of this relationship are yet to be determined, due to potential risks of the new government being seen as an outsider and military involvement facing criticism. The story also mentions a proposed 6,000-strong European force to secure Tripoli's airport and train the Libyan military. The European Union's coordination of significant portions of this assistance is also discussed, with potential training for Libyan police, coastguard, and military taking place in Libya or neighbouring countries. The Libyan government's needs will determine the extent of international assistance, which could potentially involve an expanded naval role for Britain.

The Beyond Caravaggio exhibition, a collaborative effort with the National Galleries in London and Dublin, showcases the works of Italian artist Michelangelo Merisi da Caravaggio and 30 other artists influenced by him, in Edinburgh. The exhibition highlights the revolutionary impact of Caravaggio's unconventional artistic style on his contemporaries, including works such as The Taking of Christ (1602) and The Supper at Emmaus (1601). Notably, The Taking of Christ was previously owned by a Scottish private collector but was turned down by the Scottish National Gallery in 1921. Citing frustration, curator Aidan Weston-Lewis comments on this missed opportunity. The exhibition, featuring works from artists like Ribera and Spadarino, runs from 17 June to 24 September and costs £12 for entry.

Two men, Virgilio Correia and Christopher Menaul, were sentenced to at least 16 years and 9 years respectively in prison for the murder of Wing Fu Cheung in 2015, during a robbery where they stabbed him 18 times, and the wounding of his wife, Kam-Fung. The murder was reportedly motivated by a need to pay off a drugs debt to paramilitaries. Two assistants, Gary and Lisa Thompson, were also sentenced for their roles in the case.

The County cricket tournament will undergo structural changes to reduce the number of games, create a clearer schedule, and move the T20 Blast to a more family-friendly summer holiday time slot. These changes aim to enhance the popularity of the sport among future generations and improve player development. The One-Day Cup final will be held at Lord's in July, and the T20 Blast is proposed to have more visibility on terrestrial television.

In the fourth quarter of 2014, U.S. GDP grew at an annualized rate of 2.6%, lower than the projected 3% but fuel price decreases have boosted consumer spending which rose by 4.3%, the fastest increase in nearly nine years. Economists predict that this increased spending due to gas savings will contribute significantly to the overall growth for 2014, which saw a 2.4% expansion as a whole. However, business investment showed a decline and there are concerns that the economy's reliance on consumer spending may weaken the overall growth due to a decrease in new orders and a slowdown in private sector business activity.

The failure of the Welfare Reform Bill at Stormont, which would have allowed the devolution of Corporation Tax in Northern Ireland, has led to corporations deferring investment decisions, as uncertainty persists over the tax rate and start date. This could potentially lead to reduced investment, net emigration, and increased unemployment in the region, according to Eamonn Donaghy of Grow NI.

Chris Rea, a multi-million album-selling singer-songwriter and former F1 mechanic, reminisces about his epiphany in experiencing Formula 1 first-hand after witnessing the sport on TV as a child. His journey took him from working on Eddie Irvine's car in the garage during the 1995 Monaco Grand Prix to gaining access to Wolfgang von Trips' personal archive and rereleasing his album celebrating the late F1 driver. Rea's love for F1 remains genuine, and he expresses his disappointment over the sport's current state, wishing for a return to its Mechanical roots.

Margaret Thatcher, who served as prime minister from 1979 to 1990, is remembered as a transformative figure in modern British history. She introduced significant changes, such as privatizing government-owned businesses and allowing council house ownership, which had both supporters and detractors. Among her notable achievements were the Falklands War victory, the rise of London as a successful financial center, and a record-breaking 11-year tenure. Known as the "Iron Lady" for her toughness and decision-making, Thatcher's life and legacy continue to inspire discussions and debates.

Ian Stewart Brady, convicted for the murder of multiple children in the 1960s, was denied a move to a Scottish prison as a psychiatric tribunal decided that he still requires treatment for chronic mental illness at Ashworth Hospital. The tribunal, which assessed his health needs, concluded that Brady continues to suffer from paranoid schizophrenia or another treatable disorder and it is appropriate for him to continue receiving medical treatment at the hospital.

The article discusses a disagreement between Musa Bility, the head of the Liberian Football Association, and Domenico Scala, who heads up Fifa's Ad-Hoc Electoral Committee, over Scala's eligibility to serve on the committee due to sharing nationality with one of the presidential candidates, Gianni Infantino. Bility has threatened to take the matter to the Court of Arbitration for Sport if Scala does not withdraw, citing Article 7.4 of the Electoral Regulations which states that anyone with a conflict of interest is barred from the committee. Scala and his spokesman argue that there is no conflict of interest since no incumbent president is running this time around. The article concludes that it remains to be seen whether Bility will follow through on his threat and whether Scala will step down.

A 21-year-old former swimming champion, Brock Turner, serving a three-month sentence for sexually assaulting a woman outside a Stanford University fraternity house, has been freed and intends to return to Ohio to live with his parents. He faces three years of supervised probation, including sex offender registration. Critics argue that his sentence was too lenient, with the judge citing Turner's lack of a previous criminal record and remorse as mitigating factors. The case sparked public outrage, particularly over the victim's impact statement and comments made by Turner's father. California is considering changes to the law to make probation less likely in sexual assault cases where no force is used against the victim.

Kayleigh Haywood, a teenager, was found dead in November 2015, and Stephen Beadman admitted to raping and murdering her. Luke Harlow, another suspect, is on trial for false imprisonment, grooming, and sexual activity with a child. The trial is centered around events that took place at Harlow's flat, where Kayleigh was held against her will, sexually touched, and later escaping naked, showing signs of distress. The jury also heard that Harlow had previously sought to groom other underage girls with intentions of kidnapping, getting them drunk, having sex, and keeping them at his flat.

The article explores the outcome of the recent European Union referendum in the UK, with a focus on regional differences. The north of England strongly voted for Brexit, voicing frustration with the perceived disconnect between the region and London. In Scotland, the vote led to a strengthening of the independence debate. In the Midlands, cities like Birmingham and Coventry voted for Brexit despite warnings from big businesses about the economy. Overall, the results suggest a split not just on Europe, but on perceptions of the metropolitan elite and a broader discontent amongst certain demographics.

Rail workers are planning to walk out for 24 hours from Monday evening in a dispute over pay and job security, potentially causing widespread cancellations and disruptions on various train networks, including Scotrail, Gatwick and Heathrow Express, Southeastern, Virgin West Coast mainline, East Coast line, CrossCountry Trains, Chiltern Railways, Arriva Trains Wales, and First Great Western. Talks are ongoing between union leaders and Network Rail to try and resolve the issue, but passengers are being advised not to travel unless necessary. The strike could particularly impact sports fans traveling to the Championship play-off final at Wembley on Monday.

The Rugby Football Union (RFU) is considering a plan to reduce the Six Nations tournament from seven weeks to six, potentially causing concerns over player safety, training, and the impact on player health, as it could condense the playing and training period. Additionally, there is an ongoing investigation into a controversial 2018 match between Wales and France that lasted 100 minutes, with concerns about the integrity of the game.

Scottish Labour Party Leader Johann Lamont resigned, accusing the UK party leadership of treating Scotland like a "branch office," with former Scottish Labour leaders Jack McConnell and Henry McLeish expressing anger and disappointment at the situation.

Various European football leagues concluded their seasons this weekend, with Club Brugge winning the Belgian league for the first time in 11 years, Benfica securing a third consecutive Portuguese title, Besiktas clinching the Turkish championship, Stuttgart being relegated from the German Bundesliga, and various other teams celebrating titles, promotions, and relegations. Furthermore, in Italy, Montepiaggio secured Serie A survival, and in Spain, Sporting Gijon avoided relegation, while Roma legend Francesco Totti's future remains uncertain.

The National Audit Office report finds that the Department for Education was unprepared for the financial implications of the rapid expansion of academies under the new government, resulting in a £1bn overspend from the original £7.3bn budget for academies in 2010-2012.

The government's insistence on grade C GCSEs in English and maths for key nursery workers is causing a recruitment crisis, leading to a decrease in the number of those completing Early Years Educator courses, discouraging new starters, and potentially jeopardizing the quality of childcare and the government's plan for 30 hours of free childcare. Industry leaders claim this could lead to an impending recruitment crisis, damaging the industry, and even forcing nurseries to close due to staff shortages and high agency costs. Candidates report leaving due to low pay and a lack of progression caused by the GCSE requirements. Some suggest accepting equivalent or similar qualifications, such as Functional Skills, as a possible alternative. The new childcare minister, Caroline Dinenage, has hinted at a possible shift in government thinking regarding the qualifications required for nursery workers.

The article summarizes the evolution and contradictions of Donald Trump's various positions on key issues during his political campaign, such as his support for strong interrogation Methods, the proposed construction of a wall on the Mexican border, and his opposition to Muslim immigration, among others.

In 2016, successful entrepreneurs advise business leaders to focus on clear objectives, understanding the DNA of their business, hard work, networking, finding the right people, and a passion for the endeavor. They emphasize the importance of digital mindset, customer focus, diversification, and innovation. Time management, tackling difficult tasks first, staying adaptive, and avoiding over-reliance on a single client or project are key strategies. They encourage innovation in products, resources, and administrative and financial systems. Finally, they emphasize maintaining honesty, passion, and an innovative mindset when building and leading a business.
